articles.title: Poa, AFP witnesses to testify on DepEd funds misuse
articles.summary: Three officials of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and defense lawyer Michael Poa are expected to testify on the alleged misuse of the Department of Education (DepEd)’s confidential…

blocks.text: Defense spokesperson Atty. Michael Poa urged both sides to be cautious in using terms such as "scam" that could influence public perception as the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte continues on August 26, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — Three officials of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and defense lawyer Michael Poa are expected to testify on the alleged misuse of the Department of Education (DepEd)’s confidential funds next week.

The prosecution panel said one of the witnesses, Col. Manaros Boransing II, will testify how an annual military event received no reward money or financial assistance from DepEd, even though the agency used the military activities in explaining its use of confidential funds.

Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong, a spokesman for the panel, also said the prosecution intends to revisit certifications involving the AFP and the Youth Leadership Summit, after DepEd used the activities in explaining confidential fund expenditures questioned by state auditors.

During the House inquiry in 2024, military officers whose certifications were later used in DepEd’s response to Commission on Audit findings testified that the Youth Leadership Summits were funded by the military and participating local governments and that their units received no DepEd confidential funds for those activities.
Adiong said Boransing’s testimony will be weighed together with the audit records and other evidence for the appreciation of the Senate impeachment court.
The testimony of Col. Magtangol Panopio will also focus on the issue, particularly on the AFP certification used by DepEd, even though the signatories previously said they did not know that purpose.

Prosecution adviser and spokesman Ace Barbers said the hearing should also protect the military’s institutional neutrality, as the officials’ testimonies will show whether military officers knowingly took part in the funding process or whether their signatures were used without a full explanation of the documents’ purpose.
He said the certifications matter because they may have been used to answer an audit question and support a public fund liquidation.
Meanwhile, Poa’s testimony could fill important gaps from his previous appearance before the House inquiry about the DepEd’s confidential funds, the prosecution said.
Poa served as DepEd chief of staff and spokesman while Vice President Sara Duterte was education secretary. He is now part of Duterte’s defense team and serves as defense spokesman.
The House prosecution plans to call him as a hostile witness in connection with the alleged misuse of P112.5 million in DepEd confidential funds.
Barbers said Poa’s former position placed him close to documents and official responses that the senator-judges need to understand.

articles.title: Leptospirosis deaths climb to 23 in Manila
articles.summary: The number of deaths in Manila due to leptospirosis this year has climbed to 23 following two more fatalities recorded yesterday, the city government said.

blocks.text: Commuters use an elevated walkway to cross a flooded section of a street triggered by heavy monsoon rains in Manila on August 17, 2026.
AFP / Ted Aljibe
MANILA, Philippines — The number of deaths in Manila due to leptospirosis this year has climbed to 23 following two more fatalities recorded yesterday, the city government said.

An additional 45 new cases brought the total number of leptospirosis cases in the city to 455 from Jan. 1 to Aug. 28, according to data from the Manila Health Department and City Epidemiology and Surveillance Unit.
Of the 455 cases, 155 were from San Lazaro Hospital alone. Thirteen of the 23 deaths were also from the hospital.
Ten of the 13 fatalities were male, while three were female. San Lazaro medical chief David Suplico said the age range of the deceased was between 22 and 59 years.
As of yesterday, the hospital had 157 patients with leptospirosis following 38 new admissions.

Mayor Isko Moreno previously said the surge of leptospirosis in the city is expected to rise further, citing the disease’s two-week incubation period following the severe flooding that hit Manila a week ago.
Other Department of Health (DOH) hospitals and the Philippine Red Cross are assisting San Lazaro Hospital by deploying additional manpower and bed capacity, Suplico said.

The hospital has written Moreno and the Department of Public Works and Highways to address the flooding in the hospital during heavy rains. Suplico warned that rising rainwater would force the hospital to suspend its outpatient department operations.
Meanwhile, the DOH has intensified its hospital referral system and response measures.

articles.title: PNP may form quick reaction teams vs school shootings
articles.summary: In the wake of recent shooting incidents in schools, the government is eyeing the establishment of police quick reaction forces that will respond to incidents of violence on campuses.

blocks.text: Philippine police gather at a school following a shooting in Zamboanga on August 18, 2026.
AFP / Roel Parreno

MANILA, Philippines — In the wake of recent shooting incidents in schools, the government is eyeing the establishment of police quick reaction forces that will respond to incidents of violence on campuses.

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla and Philippine National Police (PNP) chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez are studying the formation of specialized police teams that could be deployed immediately in the event of shootings in learning institutions.

Nartatez, for his part, said they are backing proposed legislation by Sen. Bam Aquino seeking to establish a sustained and coordinated approach to protecting students from threats and emergencies in school campuses.
Aquino has filed Senate Bill 2426, or the Comprehensive School Safety Act, which would establish a nationwide system for school safety.
Nartatez said they are ready to work with the Department of Education to ensure that schools remain safe spaces for students, faculty and school employees.

articles.title: Zaldy Co, 8 DPWH execs face malversation raps
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman has filed malversation and graft charges before the Sandiganbayan against former congressman Zaldy Co and eight officials of the Department of Public Works and Highways…

blocks.text: Zaldy Co.
Zaldy Co / Philstar.com's screenshot

MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Ombudsman has filed malversation and graft charges before the Sandiganbayan against former congressman Zaldy Co and eight officials of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) over an allegedly anomalous P77-million flood control project in Balagtas, Bulacan.

The ombudsman said its investigators found probable cause to charge Co and DPWH officials Henry Alcantara, Brice Hernandez, Arjay Domasig, Jaypee Mendoza, Niño Lawrence Morales, Juanito Mendoza, Floralyn Simbulan and Christina Mae Pineda with graft and malversation of public funds through falsification of public documents.
Co’s staff members John Paul Estrada and Mark Tecsay were also included in the indictment.
The charges involve the construction of a riverbank protection structure along the Balagtas River in Purok 4, Barangay San Juan, Balagtas, Bulacan.
The project was awarded to SYMS Construction Trading and had a revised contract amount of approximately P77.2 million.
The ombudsman said it was found through inspection that the structure was non-existent despite documents and certifications indicating accomplishment of the project.
“The project supposedly started last February 24, 2025 and was declared to be 100% accomplished on May 2, 2025. However, upon inspection, it was non-existent,” the resolution read.

The ombudsman, in finding probable cause, said Alcantara collected kickbacks from contractors and delivered these to Co, who ensured that the projects would be “inserted” in the National Expenditure Program prepared by the executive and eventually funded in the General Appropriations Act or the national budget.
“Co’s participation was therefore necessary or indispensable in this elaborate scheme of embezzling funds intended for flood control projects,” the resolution stated.

articles.title: Pump price rollback seen next week
articles.summary: September is set to start on a good note for motorists, with diesel prices expected to drop by P3.50 to P4 per liter next week.

blocks.text: Gasoline prices are also seen rolling back, although by a much smaller P0.25 to P0.75 per liter.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — September is set to start on a good note for motorists, with diesel prices expected to drop by P3.50 to P4 per liter next week.
The projections are based on the four-day average of Mean of Platts Singapore prices and movements in foreign exchange rates.
The final adjustments, which are expected to be announced on Monday, will still depend on the outcome of the last trading day.
Jetti Petroleum president Leo Bellas said prices fell this week amid signs that talks could resume to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key trade route for oil and gas shipments.
“Iran said it had resumed talks with Oman, although the physical supply picture reflects a still-constrained market and supply disruption risks remain,” Bellas said yesterday.
Also weighing on prices were rising regional inventories as supplies from China and India continued to increase.
However, global oil prices recently rebounded after reports that the United States was no longer interested in returning to the terms of its previous ceasefire deal with Iran.
“The potential rollback on local pump prices next week could be capped, with the risk of pushing to the lower limits of the initial estimated range,” Bellas noted.
Last Tuesday, gasoline, diesel and kerosene prices climbed by up to P1.08, P2.31 and P0.95 per liter, respectively.
The Department of Energy expects fuel price adjustments, whether rollbacks or hikes, to remain at single-digit levels in the weeks ahead.

articles.title: Missing Filipino in Nepal identified; family asks for help
articles.summary: A 30-year-old doctor has been identified as the Filipino missing in Nepal following a catastrophic flash flood that has claimed the lives of at least 489 people.
articles.byline: Andrew Ronquillo, EJ Macababbad, Michael Punongbayan, Bella Cariaso

blocks.text: A drone shot shows firefighters conducting search and rescue operations at a damaged road leading to Gyirong Port yesterday following a mudslide and flashflood in Gyirong county, Shigatse, Tibet Autonomous Region. Inset shows a Facebook image of Juan Carlos Manalo, the Filipino doctor who is currently missing after the catastrophic flash flood in Nepal.
MANILA, Philippines — A 30-year-old doctor has been identified as the Filipino missing in Nepal following a catastrophic flash flood that has claimed the lives of at least 489 people.
In a Facebook post yesterday, Chiara Manalo said her brother, physician Juan Carlos Manalo, “has been missing and out of contact since the flash flood at the Nepal border last Aug. 26, 2026.”
“Please help us look for my brother,” she appealed to the public.

Chiara said her brother’s last contact with the family was around 1 p.m. (Philippine time) on Tuesday, a day before the flash flood hit in the Bhotekoshi River, on the Nepal-China border in Rasuwa district.
In a list provided by Nepali Police, Manalo was reported to be among a group of pilgrims on their Kailashyatra tour organized by the India-based spiritual organization Isha Foundation.
“The group’s last known whereabouts was at the immigration office at Gyirong,” Chiara said, citing information from the Philippine counterpart of the pilgrimage group.
At least 77 pilgrims en route to India remain unaccounted for after the flood hit the immigration center, according to a social media post on Wednesday by Isha Foundation founder Sadhguru.
Chiara said her brother served as a volunteer medical worker at the foundation for the past couple of years and had joined the tour early this month.
“Kuya went to India in May this year for a retreat with the Sadhguru group. He mentioned that they would go to Nepal. They previously went there last year,” Chiara said.
“We humbly ask to include him in your prayers, that he may return to us safely soon,” Chiara added.
“We’re considering if we want to go (to Nepal). Realistically, we don’t know what will happen. Right now, we’re focusing on getting as much reach as possible,” Chiara said.
Juan Carlos, a general physician, is the oldest among four siblings. His interests include yoga and meditation, Chiara said.
The Department of Foreign Affairs said yesterday that the government is coordinating with the Philippine embassy in India and the honorary consulate general in Nepal to assist affected Filipinos.
Similar scenario?
Asked whether what happened to Nepal could take place in the Philippines, a disaster-prone country, Science Secretary Renato Solidum Jr. said, “not to that extent or scale.”
He, however, did not discount the possibility of another Typhoon Sendong happening in the country.
The 2011 typhoon caused up to 2,500 deaths in Mindanao as flash floods caused dams to burst.
Debris avalanches could also pose danger for people living in mountainous areas, like the tragedy that struck Saint Bernard town in Southern Leyte in 2006.
Mahar Lagmay, executive director of the University of the Philippines Resilience Institute, said many Filipinos continue to be vulnerable to debris flows.

articles.title: Monsoon to spawn weekend rains over Luzon
articles.summary: Heavy rains from the southwest monsoon or habagat are expected to affect large parts of Luzon through Monday, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration said.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Heavy rains from the southwest monsoon or habagat are expected to affect large parts of Luzon through Monday, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration said.

According to the impact-based warning of PAGASA yesterday, prolonged and widespread disruption to the daily routines of households and businesses is anticipated in parts of Bataan, Bulacan, Nueva Ecija, Pampanga, Tarlac and Zambales.

Under the “severe” level, widespread damage to houses and buildings, crops, livestock and aquaculture may occur. Road and rail transportation may also be disrupted, while health facilities, power and water services may be affected.
The warning also noted that severe injuries, permanent disability and danger to life may be expected.

As of yesterday, two low-pressure areas were being monitored by PAGASA. The first was inside the Philippine area of responsibility, last located 560 kilometers east-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, while the other was outside PAR, last located 1,460 kilometers east of Central Luzon.
Both had a medium chance of developing into a tropical cyclone within the next 24 hours.

From this afternoon until Monday afternoon, an orange warning is expected over Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Abra, Benguet and Zambales, while a yellow warning is expected over Batanes, Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Nueva Vizcaya, Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Bataan, Pampanga, Bulacan, Metro Manila, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas and Occidental Mindoro.
Class suspensions
Malacañang suspended work in government offices and classes at all levels in public and private schools in Metro Manila and 16 provinces yesterday afternoon.
The order, contained in Memorandum Circular 132 issued by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, took effect at 1 p.m.

Citing the expected further enhancement of the southwest monsoon, the suspension covered the National Capital Region, Abra, Benguet, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Bataan, Bulacan, Nueva Ecija, Pampanga, Tarlac, Zambales, Batangas, Cavite, Rizal, Oriental Mindoro and Occidental Mindoro.
Government agencies providing basic and health services, disaster preparedness and response and other vital services were directed to continue operating.
Local chief executives were also authorized to suspend classes and/or work in government offices in their areas.
In the private sector, the suspension of work or adoption of alternative work arrangements was left to management. — Bella Cariaso, Helen Flores, Aubrey Inosante

articles.title: Roblox, Meta to beef up protection vs online threats
articles.summary: Tech giant Meta and online gaming platform Roblox have agreed to strengthen their child safety measures following meetings with Philippine cybersecurity officials.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Tech giant Meta and online gaming platform Roblox have agreed to strengthen their child safety measures following meetings with Philippine cybersecurity officials.
Meta has committed to be more proactive in removing harmful artificial intelligence-generated deepfakes on its online platforms, the Philippine officials said.

The company also agreed to provide the credentials and data of users involved in online sexual abuse and exploitation of children, child sexual abuse and exploitation materials, obscene content and online abuse.

For its part, Roblox has vowed to integrate its user verification prods with the Philippine Identification or national ID system and establish a local office in the Philippines by October this year, which are the two remaining conditions the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) has set so it can continue operations in the country.

Meta representatives also vowed to respond to lawful requests from authorities investigating cybercrimes and other online threats, Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center executive director Renato Paraiso said yesterday.

“Our expectation is that these developments will translate into faster coordination, more effective investigations and, more importantly, better protection for Filipinos, especially children and other vulnerable internet users,” Paraiso said.

DICT Secretary Henry Aguda, Paraiso and other government officials met with regional executives of Meta and Roblox in Singapore following a spate of violent incidents in schools perpetrated by minors allegedly influenced by predators and groomers online.
For Roblox, the gaming platform has complied with the three other requirements – default public controls, a chat system to monitor violent tendencies and coordination with gaming communities.
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla earlier flagged Roblox for its chat group where groomers, both foreigners and Filipinos, were found to be inciting teenage users to commit violence.

The integration of Roblox’s verification process with the country’s ID system will help establish users’ identities, making it difficult for adult predators and groomers to access spaces used by children.

Paraiso said Roblox agreed to develop measures that would allow children to communicate only with users within their own age group and close loopholes that could allow adults, groomers and extremist elements to infiltrate child-focused spaces in the platform.

Paraiso said the government is also looking at additional safeguards that may be included into the guidelines and regulatory measures for online gaming platforms. They will hold a town hall meeting to get inputs from web developers.?
Meta, Phl officials to meet
Meta officials are set to meet with government officials in September to discuss information sharing protocols with law enforcers and measures against violent and abusive content on its platforms.
NBI Director Melvin Matibag said the discussions will focus on a protocol for information sharing to support case-building and investigations by law enforcement agencies.
“They themselves will go to Manila to put into writing, through a memorandum of understanding or agreement, what we want to do,” Matibag told Bilyonaryo News Channel.
The NBI chief said the talks covered recent incidents involving violence against children in Tacloban and Zamboanga, as well as online scams, abuse and deepfakes targeting public figures.

He said Meta had committed to cooperate with Philippine authorities even before a proposed law expanding the government’s authority over online platforms takes effect. Under the proposed measure, platforms would be required to provide data requested by law enforcers, he said.
‘No evidence of conspiracy, bullying’

The Ateneo de Zamboanga University (AdZU) said that results of the investigation of the Philippine National Police did not find conspiracy and bullying following the shooting on its campus that left two students dead, including the gunman.

“We have received the PNP investigation report of the Aug. 8 incident at our junior high school. AdZU cooperated fully through all the investigation and will continue to cooperate as the legal process moves forward. The report found no evidence of conspiracy or coordination with others,” AdZU president Fr. Ernald Andal said in a video message, as he confirmed that they already received a copy of the PNP report.

“It also found no evidence that bullying, disciplinary concerns, interpersonal conflict or a school-related grievance motivated the attack. This is important to note because in the days immediately after the incident, many claims about bullying, conflict in school and other supposed motives were circulated as though they were already established facts,” Andal added.

As the PNP has referred complaints for alleged reckless imprudence resulting in homicide and physical injuries against two persons, Andal noted that these matters will now go through the proper legal process.

“We respect due process and will not prejudge anyone’s responsibility. We will also extend appropriate support to affected personnel and so far as this may properly be provided,” he said. — Mark Ernest Villeza, Bella Cariaso

articles.title: P735.56 billion ‘red flag’ items spotted in 2027 budget
articles.summary: A coalition of civil society organizations has flagged P735.56 billion in President Marcos’ proposed 2027 national budget as vulnerable to political intervention and insertions, raising…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A coalition of civil society organizations has flagged P735.56 billion in President Marcos’ proposed 2027 national budget as vulnerable to political intervention and insertions, raising concerns ahead of the 2028 polls.

The People’s Budget Coalition (PBC) said these red flags consist of P140.07 billion in “soft pork” or social assistance and other programs susceptible to politicking and P483.51 billion in “hard pork,” covering infrastructure projects vulnerable to budget insertions, ghost projects and other anomalies.
The remaining P111.98 billion falls under “shadow pork,” referring to unprogrammed appropriations that the group said raise questions on transparency and constitutionality.

“In theory, or in a vacuum, these programs shouldn’t be harmful. For example, infrastructure and social protection are necessary. However, we have observed the pattern of insertions in previous years’ budgets, and from feedback on disbursement and implementation, we can see the high politicization hijacking these programs,” PBC co-convenor AJ Montesa told The STAR.
Montesa said the red flags should be monitored closely at every stage of the budget process, from the National Expenditure Program (NEP) to congressional deliberations.
While the P735.56-billion high-risk items are already identified in the executive’s proposed budget, Montesa said the red flags could become bigger once Congress begins reviewing the spending plan.

“The pattern has been for Congress to really increase these red flag items when enacting the GAA (General Appropriations Act), but the hope is that the respective budget committee chairs will be open to civil society’s feedback and monitoring,” he said, after calls from civil society organizations that they are being sidelined in budget talks.

Montesa cited Senate President and finance committee chair Sherwin Gatchalian as an example, saying he had been receptive to civil society feedback and that the Senate had required stronger documentation for infrastructure-related amendments.
“It really takes full openness and transparency to prevent budget anomalies or misallocations,” he said.
Election budget
More than P71 billion of the red flag items under “soft pork” amount is tied to government assistance programs, with proposed allocations having been sharply reduced from their 2026 levels.

In an interview with “Storycon” on One News, public finance analyst Zy-Za Suzara said while funding for such programs has been reduced from 2026 levels, they still account for a significant portion of next year’s proposed budget.

She cited programs such as the financial aid projects like the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) under the Department of Social Welfare and Development, the Department of Labor and Employment’s Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged/Displaced Workers (TUPAD) and the Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) under the Department of Health (DOH).
Suzara also flagged the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF), which she described as lump sum allocations that are discretionary in nature.

“If you look at the (proposal), you will see that the budget for human capital development… they were all cut,” she said. “What were maintained? If we look at the figures, the large amount that was maintained are for soft pork or hard pork… We can see that election is the priority.”
The AICS is proposed to receive P33.28 billion, about 48 percent lower than the P63.9 billion allocated under the 2026 GAA.
Meanwhile, TUPAD would get P14.25 billion, down 36.5 percent from P22.44 billion this year, while MAIFIP is proposed to receive P24.24 billion, a 53 percent reduction from P51.65 billion in 2026.
Montesa said these programs are prone to “pet insertions as they entrench patron-driven politics to the detriment of rules based social protection,” building political visibility ahead of the polls.

“Social protection has been hijacked as a means for politicians to create utang na loob with voters, instead of having a rights-based and rules-based system for social protection – this is patronage,” he said.

The Commission on Higher Education’s Tulong Dunong program and the Presidential Assistance to Farmers and Fisherfolk received no allocation in the proposed 2027 budget, after getting P2.73 billion and P10 billion, respectively, in 2026.
‘Ballooning LGSF’
While acknowledging the high inflation, the PBC said social protection remains important, but the payouts and disbursements should be rules-based and based on data and needs.

“Additionally, we also see an uptick in the budgets for confidential and intelligence funds, as well as for ‘local pork’ – the Local Government Support Fund,” Montesa said.?He said this is a lump-sum fund whose allocation and distribution are decided by Malacañang.

The P58.53-billion LGSF allocation forms part of the P109.13 billion earmarked for local government units in the proposed 2027 budget. This is slightly higher than the P57.87 billion in the 2026 budget.
This fund is transferred to provinces, cities, municipalities and barangays to finance priority development programs and urgent local needs.
Gatchalian has scrutinized the LGSF, which – he pointed out – historically hovered between P10 billion and P15 billion before quadrupling last year.

Department of Budget and Management (DBM) acting Secretary Kim Robert de Leon explained the ballooned fund is currently focused on two main fronts: a nationwide rice distribution program to cushion the impact of inflation and infrastructure development to stimulate local economic growth.

While De Leon cited “sustained gains” to justify repeating the massive allocation, Gatchalian demanded a concrete study proving the fund’s actual impact on countryside development and poverty reduction.
Hard pork
The biggest chunk of the coalition’s red flags comes from infrastructure.

Of the P483.51 billion in infrastructure projects that PBC classifies as “hard pork,” the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) has proposed a nearly P650-billion budget for 2027, including funding for asset preservation and flood management.

Other infrastructure-related allocations include P16 billion for farm-to-market roads, P46.36 billion for the National Irrigation Administration and P14.54 billion for the DOH’s Health Facilities Enhancement Program.
The government is seeking to ramp up infrastructure spending to support economic growth. But for the PBC, the increase also means more projects that need to be protected from political intervention.
Montesa said the group has observed patterns of anomalous infrastructure insertions in previous budgets, particularly in flood-control projects.

“Flood control projects were awarded to legislative districts with congressmen who have ties to the Speaker or President rather than being based on a master plan or a mapping of risk. This pattern has been evident since at least 2019,” he said.
Montesa also called for infrastructure projects to be backed by detailed data, including geotagging, to allow the public to track where projects are located.

Another category is the “shadow pork,” which consists of P111.98 billion in unprogrammed appropriations, generally intended to serve as standby funds subject to specified conditions before they can be released.
Among the biggest items are P57 billion for the fund restoration of the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corp. and P42.55 billion for support for foreign-assisted projects.
Montesa said unprogrammed appropriations have increasingly become a red flag since 2022, as they are increasingly prone to insertions, and the bloating of this item signifies abuse of the budget.
Confidential funds

The DBM has rejected requests for confidential funds from civilian agencies lacking legitimate surveillance mandates for the proposed 2027 national budget, amid the ongoing impeachment trial highlighting the potential abuse of secret funds.

During the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC) hearing at the Senate on Thursday, Gatchalian sought assurances that the proposed P10.7-billion allocation – comprising P4.3 billion for confidential and P6.4 billion for intelligence funds – was strictly vetted by the executive branch.
De Leon confirmed the agency filtered out requests from unqualified offices, ensuring such allocations are strictly limited to law enforcement and intelligence bodies.
Ping flags P3.2 billion lump sum
Meanwhile, Sen. Panfilo Lacson asked the DBM if it thinks the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027 is “execution ready” when it has millions in “lump sum” funds.
Speaking during the DBCC hearing, Lacson questioned De Leon for saying the 2027 NEP is “execution ready.”
Lacson said he has flagged P180 million in “lump sum” funds under the DPWH budget for the construction of evacuation centers in each region.
With 18 regions in the country, the total lump sum fund for evacuation centers stands at P3.24 billion.

“Interestingly, you (De Leon) said the budget preparation is execution-ready. There’s a program of work, etc. But we saw P180 M for each (region), a lump sum, intended for all (18) regions, evacuation centers. It doesn’t even specify at which part of the region... there are no specifics,” Lacson said.
De Leon said the agencies would be required to submit the final details to the DBM, and the Office of Civil Defense has yet to finalize the list.

At the same committee hearing, the senator also called for persistently nonperforming government-owned and controlled corporations (GOCCs) to be abolished or completely defunded to maximize the state’s limited resources.

In response, Finance Secretary Frederick Go disclosed that the Governance Commission for GOCCs is currently evaluating 21 GOCCs for closure, winding down or absorption by other state firms. — Janvic Mateo, Neil Jayson Servallos, Marc Jayson Cayabyab

articles.title: At least 93,000 ‘in great need’ after Nepal-Tibet flash floods, says Red Cross
articles.summary: Federation says it fears death toll of nearly 600 will continue to rise as rescuers reach cut-off areas
articles.byline: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Bidur, Sam Jones and agencies

blocks.text: The Red Cross has said at least 93,000 people may have been affected by Wednesday’s flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border, which have killed nearly 600 people, left another 1,900 missing, and triggered a huge rescue operation that is being hampered by fears of new flooding.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), the world’s largest humanitarian network, said it feared the death toll would continue to rise as some of the hardest-hit areas remained inaccessible after roads and bridges were destroyed by the torrents.
“The trauma of this event is enormous,” David Fisher, the IFRC head of delegation for Nepal, said on Friday.

“Thousands of homes have been destroyed or suffered significant damage. We believe that at least 93,000 people have been affected and are in great need. The death toll is very high and unfortunately likely to continue to rise.”

The deadly floods occurred on Wednesday morning after an enormous section ⁠of a glacier in the Himalayas broke loose and crashed on to the valley floor in Nepal’s Langtang national park, unleashing a massive surge of water, mud, rock and ice that thundered down rivers and valleys. The resulting floods obliterated villages and destroyed power stations, roads and bridges.

Nepal’s steep slopes and the lush valleys below are especially vulnerable to flooding and landslides, and extreme weather events, such as intense monsoons, and melting glaciers have become more common because of warming due to human-caused climate change.

“The damage is just incredible,” Lila Pieters Yahia, the UN resident coordinator for Nepal, said on Friday, adding that more than 40 bridges had been destroyed or badly damaged and “over 40km of road completely destroyed”.

By Friday afternoon, the death toll stood at 584 people: 579 in Nepal and five across the border in Tibet, China. Authorities in Nepal said 1,942 people were still missing, including hundreds of foreign nationals who were in the area to work, trek with guides or make a pilgrimage.

blocks.caption: On the ground in Nepal after deadly flash floods - video

blocks.text: Rescue teams have reported finding bodies hundreds of miles downstream from the disaster zone in the Chitwan district of Nepal, near the Indian border. Dozens of injured people were transported to Kathmandu for advanced medical care and more than 100 people were rescued by Nepali army personnel in helicopters.

Rescuers were forced to suspend operations on Friday morning after a dam of debris overflowed on Friday, increasing the risk of further flooding. Residents in Nepal’s Rasuwa district, on the border with Tibet, were seen rushing up hillsides to escape a possible surge in the river, ⁠according to witnesses.

blocks.caption: Relatives display photos of missing people outside a hospital in Kathmandu, where they have travelled from Rasuwa to seek information about family members. Photograph: Subaas Shrestha/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

blocks.text: The Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that a lake formed by piles of debris from the mudslide had begun overflowing on Friday, sending water towards the area where rescue teams were headed, and forcing a brief pause in operations.

Rescue efforts in Bidur, the capital of the Nuwakot district in Bagmati province, Nepal, were disrupted on Friday morning as the Trishuli River began to rise again after the lake near the border overflowed.
Rescue workers were moved from the area and people who had tried to return to what remained of their homes were told to evacuate again immediately.

Bidur, once a bustling town on the banks of the Trishuli, now lies in ruins. Most homes were washed away when mud, rocks and debris surged down the river valley early on Wednesday. Survivors described clinging to buildings and trees as the water rushed over them.

blocks.caption: People surveying the aftermath of the flooding in Bidur. Photograph: Ahmer Khan/The Guardian

blocks.text: The mangled concrete remains of a bank, a government office and an ATM booth were among the few structures left standing, although they were submerged in mud. Officials said there were bodies inside the buildings but it was too dangerous to recover them.
Nearby, people gathered along the muddy road, calling out for lost relatives and trying to dig out what was left of their belongings.

blocks.caption: A woman among the ruins of Bidur. Photograph: Ahmer Khan/The Guardian

blocks.text: Most areas battered by the flash floods remained accessible only by army helicopter. At the Bidur army camp, from where much of the rescue effort was being coordinated, rescue and military helicopters flew in and out every five minutes, bringing in dozens of traumatised victims. Many said the floods had taken their loved ones, their homes and everything they owned in a matter of minutes.
The international community is scrambling to get aid to flood-stricken parts of Nepal and Tibet.
Nepal has said it does not yet need foreign assistance as the search and rescue operation – complicated by the destruction of bridges and roads across the mountainous region – continues.

“The offer for help is natural,” Lok Bahadur Chhetri, a spokesperson for Nepal’s foreign ministry, said on Friday. “Our security agencies ‌are doing the search and rescue operation. For now we don’t require such help.”

The Kathmandu Post reported that India, China, the US, Britain, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh had asked the government to allow their search and rescue teams to assist in the operation.

Dinesh Bhattarai, a former Nepali ⁠ambassador to the UN in Geneva, said the government’s reluctance to ​accept foreign assistance may ​be linked to sensitivities over ​Rasuwa district and its border with Tibet.
“They may have thought about ​the locational sensitivity ‌of the region and ​decided not to ​accept foreign teams,” Bhattarai told Reuters.
But Chhetri said Nepal’s own rescue teams were handling the operation and the decision to refuse foreign assistance had nothing to do with sensitivities.

Scant information has emerged from Chinese authorities about the scale of the destruction in Tibet, the most tightly controlled part of China even under normal circumstances. Only brief, state-controlled media reports about the floods have been allowed to circulate in China and the authorities have confirmed only five deaths there. Chinese reports have focused on rescue efforts.

blocks.caption: Excavators clear debris to restore a road damaged by the flash floods on the Tibet side of the border. Photograph: China News Service/Getty

blocks.text: With Agence France-Presse and Reuters

articles.title: Pampanga prov'l gov't orders pre-emptive evacuation amid red rainfall warning
articles.summary: PAMPANGA — Authorities have ordered the immediate implementation of pre-emptive and forced evacuation in high-risk and vulnerable areas across the province amid persistent heavy to intense rains…

blocks.text: Pampanga police quickly responded to a call for help and rescued families affected by rapidly rising floodwaters in Barangay Sto. Cristo, Lubao, Pampanga on Friday. (Photo courtesy of PNP / via Liezle Inigo)

PAMPANGA — Authorities have ordered the immediate implementation of pre-emptive and forced evacuation in high-risk and vulnerable areas across the province amid persistent heavy to intense rains brought by the southwest monsoon or Habagat.

Pampanga Gov. Lilia “Nanay” Pineda, chairperson of the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (PDRRMC), ordered local officials to ensure the early evacuation of residents in areas at risk of flooding and landslides.

The directive came after the DOST-Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) issued a red rainfall warning, and possibility of serious flooding in low-lying areas and communities near rivers and waterways.
Rainfall of between 50 and 100 millimeters may be recorded until noon of Aug. 31, 2026, according to the advisory.
Such conditions may trigger or worsen flooding and landslides in vulnerable areas.
Residents were urged to immediately comply with evacuation orders from their respective local government units and barangays .
Authorities encourage residents to prepare essential belongings and emergency kits and continue monitoring official weather.
“Do not wait for the situation to worsen before evacuating,” authorities said, emphasizing that the safety of Pampanga residents remains the top priority.

articles.title: Norway’s King Harald dies aged 89
articles.summary:
Norwegians gather to remember monarch whose death comes amid scandal over links between crown princess and Jeffrey Epstein

Norwegians have gathered in their thousands to pay their respects…

blocks.text: Norwegians have gathered in their thousands to pay their respects to King Harald V, Europe’s oldest reigning monarch, who has died, aged 89, in Oslo. He was succeeded immediately by his son, King Haakon VIII.

The new king thanked “the government and Norwegian people for their support and sympathy for the royal family at this time”. A period of national mourning was announced as crowds left wreaths and messages outside the royal palace in Oslo.

Flags around the country were lowered to half mast and church bells rang out at midday. “An era has ended. A new one begins. The king is dead. Long live the king,” the prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre, said after meeting Haakon.

The new king, whose wife, Mette-Marit, has recently come under scrutiny over scandals including a much-criticised association with the late US child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, formally notified the government of his father’s death on Friday morning.

blocks.caption: People gather outside the royal palace in Oslo after the death of King Harald. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters

blocks.text: Haakon, 53, told the cabinet at an extraordinary council of state that he would take the name Haakon VIII, as expected. He also chose as his personal motto: “Everything for Norway.”

The new king will swear an oath of accession in parliament within the next few days. Coronation ceremonies were abolished in Norway more than a century ago, but Haakon could choose to have his reign blessed at a consecration ceremony.

The palace had said on Thursday that Harald’s health had deteriorated and that the king, who was seen as a unifying figure and a force for stability amid a string of recent family scandals, was in an “extremely serious” condition.

blocks.caption: King Harald during a welcoming ceremony for the Danish king and queen in Oslo in May 2024. Photograph: Per Ole Hagen/Getty Images

blocks.text: Støre said earlier that he had received the news “with deep sadness”, adding: “A whole nation is in mourning, and ⁠the people of Norway are left with a ​deep sense of ‌gratitude for a ‌long life in the service of Norway.”

Royalty around Europe sent their condolences, with Spain’s royal family hailing Harald’s “responsibility, dignity, humility and tireless dedication”, and Denmark’s King Frederik and Queen Mary saying he was “loved like few others”.

King Carl XVI Gustaf, of Sweden, said: “Throughout the years, King Harald has been a good friend to me, my family, and to Sweden … I ​wish ​my dear godson Haakon, ​who now succeeds his father as head ​of state, ‌success and ​good ​fortune.”

Belgium’s royal family recalled Harald’s “humour, humanity and sincerity”, while Britain’s King Charles mourned the loss of his “dear cousin”, paying tribute to a “towering figure” who guided his country with “warmth and humility”.

blocks.caption: People gather at Palace Square in Oslo to pay their respects to King Harald. Photograph: Rune Hellestad/Getty

blocks.text: Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz, said Norway had “lost a great figure who stood for prudence and unity”, and the French president, Emmanuel Macron, expressed “deep sadness”.

Norway’s ceremonial head of state since 1991, Harald was being treated in Oslo’s University hospital for haemolytic anaemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of the body’s red blood cells.

He had had numerous health problems – an operation for bladder cancer in 2003 and a pacemaker fitted in 2024 – but always ruled out abdicating, saying he had taken a lifelong oath before the Norwegian parliament.

His death comes amid a turbulent period for Norway’s royal family. Documents published in the US in January showed that Mette-Marit corresponded with Epstein between 2011 and 2014, long after he was convicted.

blocks.caption: Haakon had taken on additional royal duties while his father was ill. Photograph: Per Ole Hagen/Getty

blocks.text: The files appeared to contain almost 1,000 mentions of Mette-Marit, including intimate exchanges. They drew fierce public criticism, with Støre accusing her in unprecedented comments of “poor judgment”.
after newsletter promotion

Mette-Marit subsequently released a statement via the royal household expressing her “deepest regret for my friendship with Jeffrey Epstein” and apologising for “the situation that I have put the royal family in, especially the king and queen”.

blocks.caption: Mette-Marit had a successful lung transplant in July. Photograph: Lise Åserud/NTB Scanpix/AP

blocks.text: Marius Borg Høiby, 29, Mette-Marit’s son from a previous relationship, has also been in the spotlight after being sentenced in June to four years in prison for two rapes and 32 other charges, including violence against a former partner. He has appealed against the decision.

The scandals have affected public support for Norway’s monarchy, with a poll in February finding support down to 54% from 72% in 2024. Several polls found nearly half of the population felt Mette-Marit could not become queen.

blocks.caption: The royal family pictured in 2022. Front, left to right: King Harald, Princess Ingrid Alexandra and Queen Sonja. Back, left to right: Marit Tjessem, the mother of Crown Princess Mette-Marit, Crown Prince Haakon, Prince Sverre Magnus and Marius Borg Høiby. Photograph: Lise Åserud/NTB/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Harald was seen as the Norwegian monarchy’s great moderniser, revamping the crown estates and changing the way the court is run. He married Sonja, a commoner, in 1968 and welcomed two others, Mette-Marit and Ari Behn, as the spouses of his children.

A great-great-grandchild ‌of Britain’s Queen Victoria, he succeeded his father, Olav V, at the age of 54 after studying at Oxford and representing his country in sailing events at the Tokyo, Mexico City and Munich Olympics. He was widely appreciated in Norway for his unassuming lifestyle and commitment to national unity.

In an emotional speech in 2011 after the far-right extremist Anders Behring Breivik killed 77 in two terror attacks, he told his subjects that “freedom is stronger than fear” and as “a father, grandfather and spouse, I can only begin to sense some of the pain you feel. As king of the nation, I feel for every one of you.”

In a widely praised 2016 speech, he lauded diversity, tolerance and LGBTQ+ rights, saying Norwegians came from Afghanistan and Pakistan, believed “in God, in Allah and in nothing”, and included “girls who love girls, boys who love boys and girls and boys who love each other”.

blocks.caption: King Harald and Queen Sonja at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan, Italy. Photograph: Heiko Junge/Reuters

blocks.text: Mette-Marit, 53, who has a serious lung disease and had a transplant in July, was a single mother to Høiby, who was four years old when her engagement to Norway’s crown prince was announced in late 2000.

The marriage, which marked the first time in modern European history that a direct heir to a throne had brought a stepson into a royal family, caused huge controversy in Norway but was strongly backed by King Harald and Queen Sonja.

Mette-Marit acknowledged having what she described as a rebellious youth and prior drug use, holding an emotional press conference a week before the wedding in which she expressed regret for her choices and strongly condemned drug use.

articles.title: How Nepali diaspora is responding to flood disaster and how Australians can help in relief effort
articles.summary:
Nepali and Tibetan communities plan vigils and work to raise funds for recovery in ‘devastating’ time

  • Get our

blocks.text: Australia’s Nepali community plan to host vigils to remember the victims of the Nepal-Tibet flood disaster to coincide with a day of mourning, as the number of people killed continues to rise.
As Australia’s Nepali diaspora wait for the full scale of the disaster to become clear, community members are desperately waiting to hear from missing relatives and friends.

Nepali authorities said on Friday that the death toll had risen to 579, with the number missing rising sharply to more than 1,900, after massive flash floods and landslides tore through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river basins on Wednesday.
The foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, on Friday morning confirmed the number of Australians missing in the floods had increased to 39 as she unveiled a $5m support package.
Wong told the ABC that Australians who wished to donate could do so via the Emergency Action Alliance website – run by a group of Australian charities and humanitarian organisations.
Nepali Australians gathered for candlelight prayers on Thursday night and held a minute’s silence for those lost to the floods.

Dr Tilak Pokhrel, president of the Australian Nepalese Multicultural Centre (ANMC), said community organisations in Victoria would host a vigil when the Nepali government announced an upcoming national day of mourning.
“Community members just want to say we are with you for those who are affected,” he said.
“We want to have an event where we all can gather and show our solidarity to support them.
“Let’s work together, let’s pray together, and let’s go through this pain together.”

blocks.caption: Candles arranged in the shape of the Nepali flag at prayers in Rockdale, Sydney. Photograph: George Chan/AAP

blocks.text: Pokhrel said the centre would extend its opening hours for the next few days so faith leaders could provide support.
“People are waiting for the news. They are checking the news every hour,” he said.
Chudamani Sapkota, the general secretary of Non-Resident Nepali Association, said its New South Wales branch would host a candlelight vigil on Saturday evening in Sydney.
“This is devastating news for all the Nepalese diaspora,” he said.
Sapkota said the organisation was trying to support Nepali Australians seeking to locate their missing relatives.
“There’s no network, nothing at the moment,” he said. “This is a very tough time.”

Melbourne student Rakshya Pandey’s family home and two grocery shops in the Nuwakot district, hit by the flash flooding, have been destroyed. Her father, who was injured after being struck by an object in the flooding, is receiving treatment in a Kathmandu hospital.
“Whenever I see the detail of the people missing or the flood or everything, it’s just so scary, and I’m scared … I can’t do anything. I feel so helpless,” she said.
after newsletter promotion
Pandey fears there will be future flooding in Nepal.

Ashok Bahadur Dhungel, who lives in Canberra, has been trying to reach his nephew who works for the Upper Trishuli hydropower plant, which sat on one of the Nepali rivers that flooded. He said his nephew has not been online for two days.
“We hope he is still alive,” he said.

blocks.caption: Melbourne student Rakshya Pandey (far right) with her family. The family’s home was destroyed by the floods that hit Nepal’s Nuwakot district. Photograph: supplied

blocks.text: Dhungel heard through friends that his mother, who lives in the Nuwakot district, had survived. But he has been unable to speak to her due to power outages.
“She is everything to me,” he said.

Tenzin Khangsar, co-chair of the Australia Tibet Council, said the Tibetan community was “shocked and devastated” about the flooding. He said prayer events would be planned to commemorate the victims.
Diaspora community organisations are also crowdfunding for the Nepali government’s disaster relief fund.

Chiran Tiwari, president of the Nepalese Welfare Society based in Sydney, said the organisation had created a GoFundMe page to raise money for the Nepali prime minister’s natural disaster relief fund.
Tiwari said one of the welfare society’s executive member’s relatives was missing in Nepal, with the community rallying around to provide support to them.
“The situation is very sad for the community,” he said. “Everyone’s eyes is tearing so the situation is very difficult.”
On Thursday night, the ANMC hosted a candlelight multi-faith prayer night in Melbourne for people grieving the disaster.

articles.title: Battle-tested officer takes command of PNP Region 1
articles.summary: CAMP BGEN OSCAR FLORENDO, La Union — A battle-tested police commander with nearly three decades of experience in crime investigation, tactical operations and security has taken charge of the police…

blocks.text: CAMP BGEN OSCAR FLORENDO, La Union — A battle-tested police commander with nearly three decades of experience in crime investigation, tactical operations and security has taken charge of the police force in the entire Ilocos Region.
PBGen. Crisaleo Roleda Tolentino, a member of the Philippine National Police Academy “Kaagapay” Class of 1996, is the new director of the Police Regional Office 1 (PRO1).
Tolentino assumed the post following the reassignment of PBGen. Jovencio Badua as director of the PNP’s Police Community Relations.
The new Ilocos top cop brings a broad operational background to the region, having served in some of the PNP’s key frontline and specialized units.
Before taking over PRO1, Tolentino headed the PNP Maritime Group, where he handled maritime law enforcement and complex security operations.

He also served as police chief of Dumaguete City, worked with the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG), handled SWAT and police operations, and held key positions in the Aviation Security Group.
His stint with the PNP Directorate for Operations further exposed him to national-level police planning, operational coordination and security concerns.
Tolentino’s experience now faces a new test as he takes command of police forces in Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union and Pangasinan.

His immediate challenge is to turn his extensive field experience into stronger police operations, faster response to crime and security threats, and closer coordination with communities and local government units.
PRO1 personnel have welcomed Tolentino and pledged support for his leadership, particularly in strengthening professionalism, public safety and public trust.
For the new regional director, the Ilocos command is his biggest assignment yet — and a fresh test for a commander shaped by years of frontline police work. (Freddie G. Lazaro)

articles.title: Norway’s crown prince becomes King Haakon VIII after his father’s death
articles.summary: COPENHAGEN, Denmark — Norway has a new king, whose tasks will include stabilizing the Scandinavian country’s monarchy and boosting the royal family’s popularity after his wife’s…

blocks.caption: Norwegian Crown Prince Haakon looks on during a tour at the Amazon Spheres, Wednesday, April 17, 2024, in Seattle. — File photo by Associated Press

blocks.text: COPENHAGEN, Denmark — Norway has a new king, whose tasks will include stabilizing the Scandinavian country’s monarchy and boosting the royal family’s popularity after his wife’s past contacts with deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and his stepson’s rape conviction.
Crown Prince Haakon, 53, became King Haakon VIII when his father, Harald V, died Friday. Haakon’s oldest child now becomes Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra and the heir to the throne.
Haakon knows the ropes. As his father aged and his health began to fail in recent years, the prince stepped in as the country’s regent on several occasions.

Norway’s monarchy has old roots, tracing its origins to King Harald Fairhair in the ninth century. When Norway regained its independence in 1905, three-quarters of voters in a national plebiscite approved restoring the monarchy. Today, the role is largely symbolic as the power lies with an elected parliament, but the country’s royal family retains celebrity and a role in promoting the wealthy nation around the world.

Haakon is the younger child of Harald, born two years after his sister, Princess Märtha Louise. As the oldest male, however, he became heir to the throne when his grandfather, King Olav, died in 1991. The Norwegian Constitution was altered in 1990 to allow future firstborns — regardless of gender — to take precedence in the line of succession. However, it was not applied retroactively.
Haakon said in a 1998 book that as a child he dreamed of owning a toy shop, but he soon realized that his path was already paved and one day he would become king.

He holds a bachelor’s degree in political science from the University of California at Berkeley and a master’s degree in development studies from the London School of Economics and Political Science, with a specialization in international trade and Africa. In 1995, he graduated from the Royal Norwegian Naval Academy, and he also completed the Foreign Ministry’s trainee program for diplomats.

An avid surfer, skier and sportsman, he told Norwegian broadcaster NRK that if he hadn’t been a royal, he would have been a surfer. A music lover — he likes rock and rap — he attended festivals across Europe as a youth.
Haakon sought the king’s permission to marry

When Haakon met Mette-Marit Tjessem Høiby — a single mother whose son’s father had been sentenced to prison for cocaine possession — at a popular music festival in Norway in 1999, he knew it was going to be an uphill battle, especially since she also had been seen at parties where illegal drugs were used.
The country was divided. Some cheered for love, others were skeptical. The Norwegian newspaper VG wrote in 2000 that Haakon “lives closer to the people than any other heir to the throne before him.”
In a May 2000 interview with NRK, Haakon said that in the early 1990s, “a youth culture emerged in Oslo” and he acknowledged that Mette-Marit was “an active part of this environment at the time.”
“It is clear that there is relatively extravagant partying there,” Haakon said.

Nevertheless, he won permission from his father, who had also married a commoner, to wed Mette-Marit. And despite her background, the Norwegian people found much to like about this statuesque blond woman with striking eyes and a ready smile, a down-to-earth manner and an undisguised love for Haakon.

They wed in August 2001 at the Oslo Cathedral. The couple’s popularity soared thanks to a carefully cultivated blend of the common touch and the glamor and grace demanded of royalty. They were constantly on the covers of gossip magazines, yet tried to live relatively normal and private family lives.
They have two children, Ingrid Alexandra and Prince Sverre Magnus. Haakon also became the stepfather of Mette-Marit’s son, Marius Borg Høiby, who has no royal title.
Royal family’s reputation took a hit from Høiby’s trial

In June, Høiby was sentenced to four years in prison after being convicted of rape. He was found guilty of two of the four rape charges he was facing and acquitted of the other two. He was also convicted of assault and abuse in a close relationship. Høiby’s lawyers said he will appeal the convictions.

The trial unfolded amid renewed scrutiny of the royal family following disclosures about Mette-Marit’s past contacts with Jeffrey Epstein, the deceased sex offender. She has publicly apologized for the association and said she exercised poor judgment in maintaining contact with him. She isn’t accused of any wrongdoing.
In a television interview in March, she said she was manipulated and deceived by Epstein and felt unsafe during a 2013 encounter with him at his Palm Beach, Florida, mansion.

In 2018, the royal palace announced that Mette-Marit had been diagnosed with a rare form of chronic pulmonary fibrosis, meaning she sometimes must take a break from her official duties. The incurable condition made breathing increasingly difficult, she had a dry cough and fatigue, weight loss and loss of appetite. She received a lung transplant in June.

In connection with the couple’s 50th birthdays in 2023, NRK interviewed Haakon and aired an old video of him playing guitar, with Ingrid Alexandra and Mette-Marit singing, and another one where he and his children mimic the moves of a Norwegian rapper. He watched the clips and burst into laughter, saying that they showed that “I am all in.”

One task for the new king will be to shore up popular support for the royal family. While a majority of people still support it, the proportion has declined in recent years and took a battering this year as Høiby’s trial played out. Critics of Haakon’s sister, Märtha Louise, who has written books in which she claimed to have contact with angels, also blame her for the family’s reputational troubles.

Märtha Louise, who was previously married for 14 years, in 2024 wed Durek Verrett, an American who describes himself as a shaman and a healer on his website. In 2022, she announced that she would no longer officially represent the Norwegian royal house, following “many questions relating to me and my fiancé’s role.”

A poll published by Norway’s Dagbladet newspaper in late 2022 showed 68% of respondents saying they wanted to keep the monarchy. When NRK asked the same question in 2017, support for the royal house stood at 81%. /das

articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY - The Land Transportation Office–Negros Island Region (LTO-NIR), served a Show Cause Order (SCO) on a tricycle driver, who was alleged to have been involved in the assault of a…

blocks.text: The Land Transportation Office–Negros Island Region (LTO-NIR), serves a Show Cause Order (SCO) on a tricycle driver allegedly involved in the assault of a 48-year-old traffic enforcer in Himamaylan City, Negros Occidental. (LTO-NIR)

BACOLOD CITY - The Land Transportation Office–Negros Island Region (LTO-NIR), served a Show Cause Order (SCO) on a tricycle driver, who was alleged to have been involved in the assault of a 48-year-old traffic enforcer in Himamaylan City, Negros Occidental.

A recent video showing a tricycle driver allegedly punching a local traffic enforcer following a confrontation reportedly related to roadside parking, went viral and reached the LTO-NIR, leading to an investigation.
The enforcer had reportedly told the tricycle driver that it was prohibited to park in the area, but the latter allegedly got irked, leading to a commotion.
The LTO-NIR Intelligence and Investigation Unit (IIU), with the assistance of LTO Himamaylan personnel, served the SCO at the Barangay 3 People’s Hall in Himamaylan City.

LTO-NIR director Jeck Conlu reminded motorists and transport operators that compliance with traffic regulations and respect for traffic enforcers were essential in maintaining safe, orderly, and disciplined roads.
This is part of the agency’s continuing commitment to uphold road safety, ensure accountability, and enforce existing traffic rules and regulations.

articles.title: Families of 33 missing Britons rush to Nepal as fears grow of more floods
articles.summary: Desperate relatives trying to reach loved ones last seen in area where entire villages have been swept away

blocks.text: Families are rushing to Nepal to search for the 33 British nationals who are still missing, as fears mount over the risk of a second wave of flooding in the region.
The catastrophic flash floods that hit Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, thundering down valleys and sweeping away entire villages, have killed at least 538 people, while more than 1,500 remain missing.
Among them are hundreds of foreign tourists who were visiting the mountainous region, which is popular with trekkers and pilgrims for its natural beauty and religious significance.

Relatives of missing Britons have shared their devastation as they desperately try to reach their loved ones who were last seen in the Rasuwa district, where power and communication lines are down. Many are scrambling to book flights to Kathmandu, the Nepalese capital.

On Friday, authorities in Nepal and China issued warnings about the risk of a second wave of flooding. Chinese authorities said an artificial lake had formed after a mudslide hit the Tibet-Nepal border, posing a risk of “sending flood waters downstream”, according to state media. Nepal’s disaster authority said a lake that had formed after debris blocked a river at the site was also rising and ‌at risk of bursting.

blocks.caption: Barrier lake forms at base of mountains near Nepal border

blocks.text: Rescuers were forced to suspend their search for survivors, while residents who had returned to Rasuwa were told to evacuate their homes. Many were seen fleeing up the hillsides to escape a possible surge in the river.

In a video on YouTube, Jaggi Vasudev, known as Sadhguru, a spiritual leader who founded the nonprofit Isha Foundation, told followers at the foundation’s camp at Saga in Tibet, China, that 80 members of an Isha group returning from Kailash Mansarovar, a high-altitude site in ‌Tibet revered by Hindus and Buddhists, were missing, including nine British people.
Among them was Neetu Goyal Tiwari, 51. Her brother Naresh Goyal told the BBC that completing the pilgrimage was “her dream”.

Neetu’s nephew, Anmol Goyal, said she had been travelling with a friend, and that her last known location was at the immigration centre on the Tibet-Nepal border. He said she had been added to the Nepalese government’s official list of missing persons.

The family have been desperately phoning contacts in Nepal in an attempt to find her, though they increasingly believe her to still be in China. As many of them are based in India, it is difficult for them to obtain visas to search for her. Goyal said her husband and daughter remained in the UK for now.

“We’re not sure what the next second holds and what we should do from our end, because we’re trying to reach everyone we can,” he said. “She was a very fun-loving woman [and] really had a great heart. I really hope she comes back soon.”

The Telegraph reported that an NHS psychiatrist, Pravin Atmakur, 54, was leading a group of 77 pilgrims on Isha Foundation’s journey to Mount Kailash. The group’s last-known location was an immigration centre in Timure, in the mudslide’s direct path.
His wife, Manjula Atmakur, who arrived in Kathmandu to search for him on Friday, told the newspaper she was disappointed by the British government’s response to the disaster.
Fishtail Tours and Travels confirmed Leena Bector, 53, from Slough, was among 27 travellers in its group who were unaccounted for.

blocks.caption: Family members of missing flood victims look at the list of missing people at the emergency ward of the Maharajgunj medical campus in Kathmandu. Photograph: Ritesh Shukla/Getty

blocks.text: Her husband, Bhupesh Bector, told the Times he was booking the next flight to Kathmandu after the Home Office had failed to confirm whether Leena was on its missing persons list. “Even if they find her today or tomorrow, I need to be there,” he said. “She must be in trauma.”

Also missing are an A-level student from Surrey, Spandan Sahu, 18, and his father, Santosh Sahu, 46, the chief executive of the UK pharmaceutical technology company Charac; Spandan’s mother, Surabhi Manmath Padhy, 44; and sister Syna Kumari Sahu, 13.
Mahadev Semwal, a friend of Sahu’s for about 15 years, said: “I had WhatsApp communication with him on Monday: they were going to Nepal then Manasarovar in Tibet.
“When I heard on Wednesday about the flooding, I lost contact with him – when I am trying to message him it is getting delivered but not read.
“Our heart says they are safe somewhere. It’s possible because the communication is jammed.
“But when you see the videos, it is unbelievable. It feels so bad.”
Also confirmed missing was Sarada Simkhada, a senior nurse from Dartford, Kent, who left for Nepal last Saturday on a religious journey.

Deepesh Patel told the Press Association that his parents, Bipin Patel, 66, and Mala Patel, 60, from Coventry, were missing after flying to Nepal on 22 August for a pilgrimage. His brother Anant Patel told Sky News he was “shocked” at the lack of information on their whereabouts.
Vikram Kolagatla, from London, told the BBC he had not heard from his wife, Geetha Reddy. Reddy, who has two daughters aged 12 and 14, had been in Hotel Kailash in Rasuwagadh when the flooding hit.
“We’re not sure what to do. I have two little girls, and their schools are starting next week,” Kolagatla added.

Tatjana Phillips, from Folkestone in Kent, told the BBC she had not been able to contact her sister, Julija Jakovicka, who was attending a yoga and meditation retreat near the Nepal-Tibet border when flash flooding hit.
Tanay Ranjan told the BBC he had not heard from his older brother Ankit Ranjan, 39, or sister-in-law, Ankita Chandra, 35, who had gone on a pilgrimage.
Ranjan added: “We don’t know if they crossed the border … We don’t have a clue where they are. We are very much devastated.”

The tour operator Alpine Eco Trek said it had been unable to make contact with a party of 12 Britons aged 13 to 65 who had booked a tour to Mount Kailash in Tibet, and were in the vicinity when the flash floods hit.

blocks.caption: Firefighters conduct search and rescue operations at a damaged area in Gyirong county, Tibet. Photograph: cnsphoto/Reuters

blocks.text: Sunil Amin, from Croydon in south London, shared with the Daily Mail the “horrible, horrible feeling” of repeatedly trying to phone his wife, Hema Amin, 63, who was on a pilgrimage with Alpine Eco Trek from Nepal to Tibet with her sister. “I’m devastated,” he said.

The Trekkers’ Society, which organises tours across Nepal, Tibet and Bhutan, said nine UK nationals on a pilgrimage had gone missing. The organisation confirmed that four men and boys aged between 14 and 50 and five women aged 40 to 53 were unaccounted for.

Himalayan Glacier US said it had lost contact with a group of 47 guests and staff, including two Britons, who were also on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, regarded as the spiritual home of the Hindu god Shiva.
The tour operator Kailash Journeys confirmed it had not been able to account for seven UK nationals – five women and two men aged between 18 and 55 – who were travelling with it.

Leaf Holidays, which runs Himalayan treks and expeditions from Kathmandu, wrote in a Facebook post that its group of 55 travellers remained missing, including four British citizens, Tara and Babar Gurung and Thaneswar and Tejkumari Gurung, who have not been heard from since Tuesday.

Twelve of the missing British citizens were on a tour to Mount Kailash led by Nabhi Nandan Das, a 64-year-old Hindu priest who works at the Sanatan Mandir and community centre in Surrey, the Telegraph reported. He is understood to have been leading 11 Britons on a tour that was due to visit Kailash and Lake Mansarovar, two Hindu holy sites in Tibet.

blocks.caption: People wait for information about their missing relatives outside a military camp in the Trishuli area of Nepal’s Nuwakot district. Photograph: Manan Vatsyayana/AFP/Getty

blocks.text: Pramod Poudel, who runs a Nepalese street food company in Sussex, told the Daily Mail his wife, Sumitra, mother, Tulisa, brother Pradip and uncle Madav were all missing. His father, Purusottam, has been found alive.
The Non-Resident Nepali Association in the UK launched an emergency fundraising appeal on Thursday and more than £12,000 has been raised.
Rajendra Pudasaini, a nurse in Essex who is president of the Non-Resident Nepali Association UK, said Nepal was witnessing an “irreplaceable loss” and Nepal was “paying the price for global warming”.

Pudasaini told BBC Radio 4 Today’s programme that many of his family members were missing. “My godson, we found the body yesterday morning, you know, he (was) just buried under the mud at his house, and yes, lots of other dead bodies being found.”
He added: “It’s a very difficult situation to describe, actually.”

articles.title: How vaccines also protect children from heart conditions
articles.summary: Vaccines do not just prevent several diseases; they can also improve a child"s heart health, according to a cardiologist from the Philippine Society of Pediatric Cardiology (PSPC).

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 11:44pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
Vaccines do not just prevent several diseases; they can also improve a child’s heart health, according to a cardiologist from the Philippine Society of Pediatric Cardiology (PSPC).
During the Philippine Heart Association’s (PHA) talk series Usapang Puso sa Puso, PSPC vice chair Dr. Maria Conception “Connie” Sison stressed the importance of vaccinating children.

“Hindi lang ito para sa pagpe-prevent ng viral infection. Pero dahil itong viral infection na ito ay puwede ring makaapekto sa puso, makapag-produce ng pamamaga or inflammation ng, ah, muscle ng puso tulad ng myocarditis, ay 'pag na-prevent itong infection na ito, ay mape-prevent din yung pagka-involve ng puso ng bata,” Sison said.

(It is not just to prevent a viral infection. Because a viral infection can affect the heart by producing an inflammation of the heart, like in myocarditis, but if this infection is prevented, it could also prevent the effect on the child’s heart.)
Amid the misinformation surrounding vaccines, Sison urged parents to trust in them.
Vaccines went through extensive testing and vetting by experts, she said.
If there are doubts about vaccines, parents should avoid turning to social media sites like Facebook or YouTube for information. Instead, they should turn to reliable sources like the PHA.
Sison also told parents to consult their doctors if they want to know more about vaccines.
It is very rare to have a contraindication to vaccinating children, Sison said. Side effects such as headaches and fevers should not dissuade parents from vaccinating kids.

The vaccination process takes into account the medical history of their child, so parents will be properly advised by their doctor, she explained. If there are side effects, the doctor will also inform them.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: ''Hindi ko na papatulan': Ortega dismisses Padilla’s 'off-topic' remarks on heroes' aliases in VP Duterte trial
articles.summary: House Deputy Speaker La Union 1st district Rep. Paolo Ortega V described as "off-topic" the controversial interjection made by Senator-judge Robin Padilla during the last Senate impeachment hearing…

blocks.text: House Deputy Speaker La Union 1st district Rep. Paolo Ortega V described as "off-topic" the controversial interjection made by Senator-judge Robin Padilla during the last Senate impeachment hearing wherein he brought up the aliases of Philippine revolution figures.
“Parang wala namang bayaning chichirya ’yung pangalan. Parang nakakainsulto naman po ’yun,” Ortega said during an online press briefing Friday, Aug. 28.
(There doesn't seem to be a hero named after junk food. That seems insulting.)

Last Wednesday, Aug. 26, Padilla tried to liken the rather questionable-sounding names appearing in impeachment trial respondent Vice President Sara Duterte's confidential fund records to the nom de guerre or assumed names of Filipino heroes and revolutionaries.

Padilla cited Jose Rizal’s “Dimasalang,” Emilio Jacinto’s “Tikbalang,” Andres Bonifacio’s “Maypagasa” and Marcelo H. del Pilar’s “Siling Labuyo” as examples of pseudonyms used during the revolutionary period.
The actor-turned-senator also cited “Marcial Bonifacio", the name used by former Senator Benigno “Ninoy” Aquino Jr. when he returned to the Philippines from exile in 1983.
For Ortega, this had nothing to do with Duterte's ongoing impeachment trial.
“Off-topic po ’yan. Siguro hindi ko na po papatulan, saka magre-react. Sobrang off-topic po sa pinag-uusapan sa impeachment,” said the Ilocano.
(That’s off-topic. I think I won’t bother responding or reacting. It’s completely off-topic from what’s being discussed in the impeachment.)
Padilla was earlier criticized for making interjections or manifestations that didn't appear to be relevant or were connected at all to the impeachment trial.

The deputy speaker's mention of "junk food" was a reference to Duterte confidential fund recipients “Mary Grace Piattos,” “Nova", “Oishi” and “Tempura". These names prompted lawmakers back in 2024 to collectively refer to some of the supposed recipients as the “Chichirya gang" during a House investigation.

Respondent Duterte is being accused of misuing P612.5 million worth of confidential funds released to the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and Department of Education (DepEd). To liquidate the funds, these agencies submitted to the Commission on Audit (COA) acknowledgment receipts (ARs) that bore the alleged fictitious names.
The amount consists of P500 million released to the OVP and P112.5 million to the DepEd)while Duterte headed both agencies.

The prosecution has clarified on Wednesday that it has not claimed the questioned names were aliases, stressing that the real issue is whether or not the identities of the supposed recipients can be established and the use of public funds properly accounted for.
It further alleges that irregularities in the supporting documents, along with other testimonial and documentary evidence, form part of the confidential fund charge against Duterte.
