articles.title: PNP joins US in explosion investigation training
articles.summary: The US Department of State"s Antiterrorism Assistance oversaw a training session that taught 24 members of the Philippine National Police (PNP) how to better investigate explosions.

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 11:26pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
The US Department of State’s Antiterrorism Assistance oversaw a training session that taught 24 members of the Philippine National Police (PNP) how to better investigate explosions.
In a statement from the US Embassy, members of the PNP and their US counterparts participated in the first Post-Blast Investigation (PBI).

“The partnership between the United States and the Philippines is a counterterrorism success story, and this graduating class reflects the continued commitment of both our nations to address current and future security challenges,” said Jonathan Loden, Senior Regional Security Officer at the US Embassy in the Philippines.
The two-week course consisted of the US representatives teaching their best practices in investigating bomb scenes.
The personnel also took part in field exercises to prepare for real situations.

“The knowledge and skills we gained here are not simply lessons that we leave behind when we return home. They are responsibilities that we must carry with us and apply properly whenever our duties require them,” said PNP Maj. Christopher dela Cruz, who partook in the training.
The PBI is a part of a series of courses facilitated by the US through the Antiterrorism Assistance program. The program has seen 10,000 Filipino law enforcement participate since 2006.

The US Antiterrorism Assistance program will conduct 120 courses, with 2,000 participants from the PNP from October 2026 to September 2027. These training sessions will also include crisis response and counterterrorism skills. —Jean Mangaluz/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Kai Sotto denies Jordan as Gilas Pilipinas gets World Cup bid back on track
articles.summary: Kai Sotto caps a prolific performance with the win-sealing block as Gilas Pilipinas noses out Jordan in overtime to start the fourth window of the FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – It probably is not coincidence that Gilas Pilipinas rediscovered its winning ways just when Kai Sotto came back.

Sotto capped a prolific performance with the win-sealing block as the Philippines nosed out Jordan in overtime, 82-81, to start the fourth window of the FIBA World Cup Asian Qualifiers at the Mall of Asia Arena on Friday, August 28.

Back in national team duty for the first time in two years, the 7-foot-3 Sotto produced a double-double of 18 points and 14 rebounds to go with 2 blocks, the last of which allowed the Nationals to snap a four-game skid and improve their record to 3-4 in Group E.

A five-second inbound violation by Scottie Thompson with less than 10 seconds left kept the comeback door ajar for Jordan, but Abdullah Olajuwon saw his potential game-winning shot layup swatted away by Sotto.
Heroes were aplenty for Gilas Pilipinas as Kevin Quiambao and CJ Perez hit big baskets down the stretch, rising to the occasion in the absence of injured naturalized star Justin Brownlee.

Perez scattered 14 of his 16 points in the fourth and overtime periods and also tallied 4 rebounds and 2 steals, while Quiambao finished with 14 points, including a gutsy three-pointer that gave the Filipinos an 82-79 lead with 13 seconds remaining.

Dwight Ramos also supplied 14 points, 5 rebounds, and 3 assists in the win, which saw the Philippines fight back from a 17-point deficit following a red-hot start by Jordan fueled by former NBA player Jalen Harris.
Harris went 3-of-3 from beyond the arc in the opening quarter as Jordan mounted a 28-14 lead before being neutralized the rest of the way.
The leading scorer of the Asian Qualifiers with an average of 27.0 points going into the game, Harris got limited to 19 points on 6-of-22 shooting.
Up next for the Philippines is Iran on Sunday, August 30, at the same venue.

articles.title: Tropical Storm Dolly downgraded to ‘open tropical wave’ as it heads to Caribbean
articles.summary:
Remnants from tropical storm could cause heavy rainfall on Leeward Islands and affect Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico and Hispaniola

Remnants of Tropical Storm Dolly, which has been downgraded…

blocks.text: Remnants of Tropical Storm Dolly, which has been downgraded to an “open tropical wave”, were moving still across the Atlantic Ocean toward the Leeward Islands, and could bring heavy rainfall to parts of the Caribbean this weekend, the US National Hurricane Center (NHC) said on Friday..

Dolly, which formed on Thursday, had maximum sustained winds of near 40mph (65km/h) with higher gusts on Friday morning. Later on Friday, forecasters said that Dolly was no longer a Tropical Storm, and had “become an open tropical wave”.

In an update on Friday headlined “Remnants of Dolly”, the NHC warned that “heavy rains from the remnants of Dolly could affect the Leeward Islands late on Saturday into Sunday with possible impacts in the Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico, and Hispaniola Sunday and Monday.”
“This heavy rain may produce flash flooding within areas of higher terrain of the Leeward Islands,” it added.

No coastal watches or warnings are currently in effect. The Leeward Islands stretch from the Virgin Islands to Guadeloupe, with the Caribbean Sea on their west side and the Atlantic to the east, while Hispaniola is the island where Haiti and the Dominican Republic are located, east of Puerto Rico.

The storm’s name has drawn unusual attention online, with observers noting that it formed just days after the death of the country music star Dolly Parton in the US earlier this week and wondering whether it was named in her honor. However, the name is a coincidence and has no connection to Parton’s death. Tropical storms are assigned names from predetermined alphabetical lists managed by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

For the names of storms in the Atlantic, there is a list of male and female names which are used on a six-year rotation. Dolly is the fourth name on the 2026 list, making it the fourth named storm of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season.

Earlier this summer, Tropical Storm Arthur brought heavy rainfall to the US Gulf coast, while Tropical Storm Bertha made landfall in Louisiana, bringing rain and strong winds. Earlier this month, another storm, Tropical Storm Cristobal, formed but quickly dissipated.
The Atlantic hurricane season runs from 1 June to 30 November. So far, the season has been quieter than usual, with experts pointing to several factors.
after newsletter promotion

“Tropical storm activity in the Atlantic basin is expected to be tempered by El Niño conditions, which first emerged in the equatorial Pacific in June,” according to forecasters with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. “El Niño increases wind shear, which tends to prevent tropical storms from forming or from getting stronger once formed.”

articles.title: Germany: Man gets life in jail for US tourist's rape, murder
articles.summary: The crime was unsolved for over three decades before new DNA proof made it possible to arrest and convict the now 81-year-old. His victim, Amy Lopez, was 24 at the time of her murder.

image.caption: The defendant had been known to authorities for other sexual offenses, including attempting to rape a 16-year-oldImage: Thomas Frey/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: A German court on Friday sentenced an 81-year-old man to life in prison for the rape and murder of a US tourist over 30 years ago.
Amy Lopez was 24 when she was raped and killed by the convicted man in 1994.
Hans S., whose last name is not given as per Germany's privacy laws, was only arrested earlier this year, when police were finally able to identify him using new DNA technology.
What do we know about the US tourist's murder?

Lopez's body was found near the historic Ehrenbreitstein Fortress in Germany's western city of Koblenz in September 1994 by children playing in the area. Her corpse bore stab wounds, severe head injuries and injuries consistent with strangling.
The regional court in Koblenz found that Hans S. had lured her into a secluded building, falsely promising to show her the way to a hostel, only to tie her up, rape her and then stab her nine times.
The court found that Hans S. had been "looking for a victim to rape" and that Lopez "was tragically in the wrong place at the wrong time."
The defendant confessed to the crime in general terms.
The courtroom was full of observers right through to the final day of what the judge called an "extraordinary case." Among those in attendance, were Amy's father and brother.
"Of course, the verdict cannot undo what happened, nor can it bring Amy back," said lawyer Kathrin Kienle, who represented the victim's family.
"But Amy's father and brother have told me that, in fact, they were never able to find any inner peace throughout this whole time whilst the perpetrator remained at large."
How was the defendant identified after 30 years?

The defendant had been known to authorities for other sexual offenses, serving prison sentences that lasted up to several years. Some of the incidents took place after 1994, with the most recent being in 2005.
His DNA had been on file since his 1999 conviction of attempting to rape a 16-year-old girl.
Though the genetic date had been later deleted, police managed to obtain a new saliva sample from the suspect, which matched a DNA trace found on Lopez's clothing.
His lawyer said he voluntarily provided the DNA sample because "he finally wanted clarity," describing his crime as "an enormous burden" on him.
The defendant was arrested at a nursing home in Koblenz at the end of February 2026.
After the verdict, defense lawyer Volker Klein said he did not intend to lodge an appeal or seek a review.
Edited by: Rob Turner

articles.title: People from over 30 countries missing after Nepal, China floods
articles.summary: Catastrophic flash floods in a border area of China and Nepal have killed at least 472 people and left more than 1,500 people missing as of Friday morning. Hundreds were foreigners in the area to…

blocks.caption: Damaged houses stand precariously near the swollen, debris-choked banks of the Trishuli River after flash floods in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026. — Photo by Associated Press

blocks.text: Catastrophic flash floods in a border area of China and Nepal have killed at least 472 people and left more than 1,500 people missing as of Friday morning. Hundreds were foreigners in the area to work, take guided treks or make a pilgrimage to a sacred Hindu site.

Thousands have been rescued, with some of the injured taken to hospitals in Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu. The number of missing from Wednesday’s disaster may vary because of progress in the ongoing rescue efforts and differences in how data was collected and verified among agencies.
A look at how multiple countries have been affected:
Nepal

Nepal’s disaster management authority said Friday morning the death toll rose to 469, with 977 people missing. The authority said 3,253 people have been rescued by helicopter, and more than 150 of the injured were taken to hospitals in Kathmandu and the districts of Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading.

Local reports cited the National Emergency Operation Center as saying Thursday the missing included 113 Nepali tourists, 85 security personnel from the army and police as well as 161 residents from the Rasuwa district and one from the Nuwakot district.
China

State media reported Thursday at least three people died and 558 were missing in Gyirong County, Tibet. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that 260 of the 558 missing people were foreigners. In addition, nearly 100 Chinese citizens were missing on the Nepal side, China’s foreign ministry said.
India

India’s External Affairs Ministry said 288 Indian nationals remain uncontactable. They included 73 people who were working on a power project. Nepal officials have said many Indian tourists were on pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus.
United States
The U.S. State Department said 90 Americans were unaccounted for in China and Nepal. It said it was not aware of any U.S. deaths. Three Americans have been rescued.
Malaysia
The board said 51 Malaysians were missing.
Ukraine

Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry said that 55 Ukrainians are missing. The number includes two tourist groups of 47 and seven people, in addition to one Ukrainian woman traveling with a foreign tour group, the ministry said.
Australia
The Australian government said 39 Australians were missing.
Britain
The board said 33 of the missing were from Britain.
Canada
Nepal’s tourism board said 25 of the missing were from Canada.
South Korea
South Korean government officials said nine citizens working on building a hydropower plant in Nepal were missing.
Singapore
Eight Singaporeans were missing, according to Nepal tourism board.
Germany
Nepal’s tourism board said eight tourists from Germany were missing.
Russia
The Russian Embassy in Nepal said eight of its citizens were missing.
South Africa
The board said six South Africans were missing.
Latvia
The board said six tourists from Latvia were missing.
Japan
Japanese media said the five Japanese tourists missing are a couple and their children.
New Zealand
Five people from New Zealand were missing, said Nepal’s tourism board.
France
The board said four French citizens were missing.
Belgium
The board said three from Belgium were missing.
Spain
The board said three visitors from Spain were missing.
Others

The board said two people each from Italy, Kazakhstan, Portugal, Ireland and Netherlands were missing. It said 10 others — one each from Belarus, Finland, Hungary, Israel, Lithuania, Philippines, Bulgaria, Switzerland, Serbia and Sweden — were also missing. /das

articles.title: Alan Peter Cayetano seeks 2026 spending update amid 2027 budget review
articles.summary: Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano has sought updates from the government"s economic team on the utilization of the 2026 national budget as the Senate begins scrutinizing the proposed…

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 11:06pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano has sought updates from the government’s economic team on the utilization of the 2026 national budget as the Senate begins scrutinizing the proposed P7.2-trillion budget for 2027.

According to Cayetano’s office, the minority leader wrote to Senate Finance Committee chairman JV Ejercito on Thursday, August 27, seeking details on how much of the 2026 budget has been spent, where the funds went, and how much the government has borrowed.
Cayetano said the information would help senators assess the proposed 2027 budget and ensure that the process is transparent and “faithful to the priorities they all promised to serve.”
“There is no measure this Congress passes each year that is more consequential and touches more Filipino lives than the General Appropriations Act,” Cayetano said in the letter.
“It is our values and priorities written in numbers. That is why we owe it to our people to get this budget right,” he added.
On Thursday, the Marcos administration’s economic team presented the proposed P7.2-trillion budget for 2027 to the Senate, as laid out in the National Expenditure Program (NEP).

During a briefing led by the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC) before the Senate Committee on Finance, the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) said it received more than P11 trillion worth of agency proposals when it prepared the 2027 NEP.

Aside from details on 2026 spending, Cayetano also asked whether funds under the government’s Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport (UPLIFT) framework had reached their intended beneficiaries.
The minority leader also sought details on the national government’s total debt as of July 31, 2026, as well as the loans and bonds it had contracted or guaranteed over the past three years.
He also asked which foreign loans and grants were still pending government approval.
Cayetano likewise requested a list of funds that had been transferred, realigned, or added to other programs since July 2023, including details on the sources and destinations of the funds.

He asked concerned agencies to immediately submit their responses and supporting documents so senators would have sufficient time to review them ahead of the committee hearings on the proposed 2027 budget. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Charles Perrottet becomes Icac’s main character amid claims of hidden payments and political hit jobs
articles.summary:
The brother of former premier questioned over what, if anything, was done in return for $2m from developer turned fugitive Jean Nassif

  • Get our

blocks.text: Finally, we are hearing from one of the central characters, Charles Perrottet, in a saga that has occupied the Independent Commission against Corruption (Icac) for nearly four years.

It began with the dismissal of the Hills Shire council and a late night 2022 speech in NSW parliament alleging secret payments from a developer. It pirouetted to a pressure campaign allegedly to remove the then NSW building commissioner, and ended with real world impacts: defective high-rise buildings and thousands of unhappy homebuyers, with the developer nowhere to be seen.
Charles Perrottet, brother of the former NSW premier, Dominic Perrottet, finally began giving evidence late Friday.

He told the commission that he had met the Toplace developer, Jean Nassif, now a fugitive in Lebanon, in December 2019 and had, over several years, provided him with advice on how to progress his developments.
Charles and Nassif bonded over their “frustrations” with David Elliott, the former member for Baulkham Hills, and a key figure in the rival centre-right faction of the Liberals, Charles told Icac.
“He was frustrated with a number of things. I would listen to him, I would appease him, because I wanted information from him,” Charles said.

Elliott had opposed some of Nassif’s developments in the Hills Shire area, earning the developer’s ire. Charles, for his part, was angry about Elliott’s attempts to unseat his brother Dominic and was looking for information on him.
Despite having a full-time job at BP as head of strategy, Charles was remunerated for his advice, though not directly.
“Jeremy [Greenwood, one of the Reformers] wanted to know if I wanted to share in their success,” Charles Perrottet said.
“I said, I have a full-time job. I didn’t want to be paid. I said, you can continue to pay Anita [Perrottet’s wife] and look after her.”

blocks.caption: Sydney property developer Jean Nassif, who is now a fugitive in Lebanon. Photograph: NSW police/AAP

blocks.text: Icac is investigating whether Nassif paid $2m in an undeclared political donation to a group of Liberal-aligned conservative men known as the Reformers, including Greenwood and Christian Ellis, in the pursuit of certain political outcomes.

In the first weeks of its investigation it focused on how these allegedly illegal donations were allegedly used to fund this group and stack branches with highly conservative members, and ultimately shift the Liberal party to the right.
But this week the inquiry has focused on a potentially far more serious issue from a public policy perspective: what, if anything, was done, primarily by Charles Perrottet, for the $2m from Nassif?
People like Charles Perrottet are not registered lobbyists. They do not appear in ministerial diaries because meetings on “political matters” with ministers do not have to be disclosed.

They can engage casually with key ministerial staff because meetings with staff don’t need to be disclosed anywhere. Many of those working for ministers have their own ambitions within the party and would be flattered by the attention.
First the good news: Icac works, but slowly
The inquiry might have taken four years to get off the ground but now we are seeing why.
Icac is painstakingly testing allegations of hidden payments made to Liberal operatives allegedly for consulting, and outcomes that were either delivered or sought from the Perrottet government.

Icac has gone through phone records, text messages, WhatsApp messages, mobile phone tower information, bank records, computers, tax returns and flight records, to track the movements of the key players and the money flow.
They even obtained CCTV footage of the main persons of interest meeting up in a hotel.
More challenging is establishing whether there is any nexus between payments and political outcomes.

blocks.caption: David Chandler speaks to the media at a building site in Sydney in 2023. Photograph: Jenny Evans/AAP

blocks.text: Former builder commissioner David Chandler gave evidence this week of a whisper campaign, which he believed was aimed at ministers and the media, to have him removed.
Chandler, a 40-year veteran of the construction industry, is not under investigation by Icac.

A former minister, Eleni Petinos, gave evidence that she believed she was “used” in that campaign. She also said she believed she was sacked precipitously by the premier and that she thought there was something else at play. Petinos is not under investigation by Icac.
We’ve also heard about Hills Shire Liberal councillors being disendorsed and replaced by a committee of the state executive of the Liberal party.
Charles Perrottet and other Reformers occupied key positions on the committee.
The old Hills council had been opposing a Toplace development at Cherrybrook.
And of course Elliott lost his seat in parliament.
Conflicts of interests
The Reformers and others involved, like Anita Perrottet, deny that these payments were nefarious and argue instead that they actually did real consulting or lobbying work.

Charles Perrottet’s wife, Anita Perrottet, was paid $313,500 from lobbying company Beckington for 18 months in 2021 and 2022 for Greyhounds NSW work and $347,000 in 2022 in “project consulting fees” in the space of three months, “for being a sounding board” for Greenwood and JPG Advisory on Catholic Cemeteries Trust.
“That’s $660,999, that’s an enormous amount of money?” said counsel assisting, Peggy Dwyer SC.
“I believe that is what I was worth. Jeremy believed I was a huge value-add,” Anita replied.

blocks.caption: Anita Perrottet gives evidence at an Icac hearing on Friday. Photograph: Icac/AAP

blocks.text: Anita Perrottet nominated three clients: Greyhounds NSW, while engaged by Beckington, and Catholic Cemeteries Trust and a vaping company, whose name she could not recall, for JPG Advisory,
“A sounding board on what?” Dwyer asked.
after newsletter promotion
Anita said her advice was entirely oral and delivered during face-to-face meetings with Greenwood or using her husband’s phone.
But she “could not recall” a single detail of her advice. By the end of her two days in the witness box she had said the phrase more than 500 times.

Icac has been unable to uncover a single document relating to these clients other than invoices issued by Anita’s company, Macquarie Consulting. No research, emails, marketing strategies or even a text were uncovered.
This was 2022, the same time as the NSW premier Dominic Perrottet and his cabinet were debating whether to merge the Catholic-owned cemeteries with the state-owned cemeteries.
The Catholic Cemeteries Trust was vigorously resisting the merger.

The Catholic Cemeteries Trust was very successful. Despite the issue coming before cabinet several times during 2021 and 2022 and an independent report describing the situation as urgent, the Perrottet government declined to act.
Dominic Perrottet did not respond to requests for comment regarding disclosures of family ties to cabinet.
Do you know Jean Nassif?
At first Anita Perrottet denied that she knew Jean Nassif or that Toplace was a client.
But in true Icac style, the bomb was about to drop.

She was shown texts about a lunch at Nassif’s house. She said she didn’t remember her husband attending the lunch, but was shown photographs of her children playing at Nassif’s house and texts showing she suggested her husband pick up a bottle of wine to take.
Anita was shown a detailed email she allegedly sent to Antony Anisse at another Liberal-aligned lobbying firm, Premier National, regarding a Toplace development in Epsom Road, Rosebery,

The development was facing delays in getting its final occupancy certificate and the email purported to outline an eight-point plan to overcome the difficulties. Anita was unable to say even what some of the acronyms she had allegedly used meant.
Dwyer put to Anita that she was being put in “an impossible position” and that she was attempting to cover for her husband, who in fact, was working for Nassif. Anita denied she was lying.
“It was a transparent attempt to create a cover for a sham arrangement that had been established by Charles,” Dwyer said. “No,” said Anita.
‘You understand that there is an offence committed if you lie to Icac,” Dwyer said. “Yes,” Anita said.
What did the premier know about his brother
When he appeared at Icac, former cabinet minister David Elliott described Dominic and Charles Perrottet’s relationship as “joined at the hip”.
Dominic Perrotet is not a person of interest.
Chandler gave evidence that Dominic Perrottet had begged him to stay on as commissioner, which was exactly the opposite of what Nassif wanted.
“I went up and had a cup of tea with the premier and he said: “David, you’ve heard the sentiment of the members and myself and we would like you to reconsider,” he told Icac this week.

blocks.caption: Dominic Perrottet speaks to the media in Parramatta in 2023. Photograph: Louise Kennerley/AAP

blocks.text: On the other hand we saw texts that indicate Charles was intimately involved in securing the NSW premiership for his brother.
In October 2021, Dominic Perrottet became premier after the surprise resignation of Gladys Berejiklian.
In the Independent Commission Against Corruption on Friday we got a rare glimpse into the frantic manoeuvreing to secure him the leadership and the key people involved in the number wrangling.
One was Charles Perrottet, the NSW Liberal party right-faction power broker and younger of Dominic, Icac heard.
In text messages he and his wife, Anita, discussed his role: “Well, it’s definitely true that he couldn’t have done it without you!!” Anita texted.
“But hopefully, you can work together now and going forward to both achieve your goals. Does he feel bad about Kean?”
Charles replied: “Yep, I told him what he needs to do there.”
Matt Kean had had an agreement with Dominic to become his deputy leader, in return for delivering moderate votes, but ultimately appointed Stuart Ayres.
They also discussed pushing council matters with the premier, and also getting rid of David Elliott.

“That’s a call for tomorrow. I told him to turn his phone off and savour the moment with Helen, as tomorrow and Tuesday is going to be crucial in showing unity, we execute the prick as soon as party room is over.”

articles.title: Norway’s King Harald V dead at 89 – palace
articles.summary: OSLO — Norway’s King Harald V, Europe’s oldest reigning monarch, died on Friday age 89, the royal palace announced. READ: Norway holds its breath as King Harald’s health deteriorates…

blocks.caption: King Harald V of Norway (R) poses for a photo with French President Emmanuel Macron in the Bird Room at the Royal Palace in Oslo on June 23, 2025, during a reception as part of the French president’s official visit to Norway. Norway’s King Harald V, Europe’s oldest reigning monarch, died on Augus…

blocks.text: OSLO — Norway’s King Harald V, Europe’s oldest reigning monarch, died on Friday age 89, the royal palace announced.

“It is with deep sadness that we announce that His Majesty King Harald passed away today. King Harald passed away peacefully at Oslo University Hospital on Friday, Aug. 28 at 6:35 a.m.,” it said in a statement.
The flag at the royal palace in Oslo was lowered to half-staff, an AFP reporter at the scene said.

Europe’s oldest reigning monarch, King Harald, had been in a hospital in Oslo since Aug. 17, suffering from hemolytic anemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of red blood cells that leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.
The royal family had rushed to his bedside on Thursday as the palace announced that Harald’s condition was “extremely serious.”
His wife, Queen Sonja, Haakon and his wife, Mette-Marit, and their adult children spent much of Thursday at his bedside, with media reporting that Haakon kept vigil overnight.
The public streamed to the palace in central Oslo for a second straight day Friday, laying flowers on the ground and huddling in groups.
Kaspara Bolstad, 24, told AFP Harald had been “a very steady and warm king.”

“I think the entire Norwegian people see him as a role model and as someone who brings people together. Whether you’re for or against the monarchy, I think he’s well-liked across the board,” she said.
Magnus Skaugseth, 27, agreed.

“He was so inclusive and committed to having values that are inclusive in the society we live in today. When there is so much division and polarization, he was a pillar pointing in the opposite direction.”
Harald, who ascended the Norwegian throne in 1991, had had multiple health problems in recent years, forcing him to have a pacemaker fitted and to scale back his official schedule.
But he always ruled out abdicating, arguing that he took a lifelong oath before the Norwegian Parliament.
Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store had canceled a work trip to Germany early Thursday due to the king’s deteriorating condition.
Turbulent year
The past year has been a turbulent one for the Norwegian royal family.
In February, King Harald was hospitalized for an infection and dehydration in Tenerife, where he was on a private trip with Queen Sonja.
His wife, also 89, was briefly admitted to a hospital in May due to heart problems.
Haakon’s wife, Mette-Marit, is under scrutiny for her ties to the late U.S. sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Documents published in January in the United States revealed her sustained and at times intimate correspondence with Epstein between 2011 and 2014, at a time when the American financier had already been convicted.
Mette-Marit’s son from a relationship prior to her marriage to Haakon, Marius Borg Hoiby, is also in the spotlight as a result of his legal troubles.
He was sentenced in June to four years in prison for two rapes and 32 other charges, including violence against a former partner. He has appealed the verdict.
Suffering herself from a serious lung disease, Mette-Marit, 53, had to undergo a lung transplant in July.
The royals remain broadly popular with the Norwegian public, in large part because of Harald’s unifying status and his unassuming, modest lifestyle. /das

articles.title: Quiambao clutch trey, Sotto game-saving block lift Gilas over Jordan in OT
articles.summary: Fans raved through the bad weather and came in droves expecting a thriller. Gilas Pilipinas gave them a game to remember. The Nationals weathered the hot start from Jordan and then leaned on heroics…

blocks.text: Fans raved through the bad weather and came in droves expecting a thriller. Gilas Pilipinas gave them a game to remember.

The Nationals weathered the hot start from Jordan and then leaned on heroics of CJ Perez, Kevin Quiambao and Kai Sotto to hack out a much-needed 82-81 overtime victory in the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asia Qualifiers at the Mall of Asia Arena on Friday, Aug. 28.

With the game tied, 79-all, Quiambao nailed a booming triple with 11.7 seconds left to put Gilas back on the driver seat before Sotto got the game preserving block on Abdullah Olajuwon just as the shot clock expired.

Perez took charge for Gilas in the final frame and overtime, scoring all of his 16 points during that stretch while Sotto announced his return to national duty with 18 points, 14 rebounds and two blocks.
Quiambao and Dwight Ramos chipped in 14 as Gilas improved to a 3-4 record in the Group E standings while Jordan slid to a 5-2 record.

Gilas found itself trailing early, 26-8 behind the blistering shooting of the Falcons, who had 10 triples in the first half. The Nationals got their bearings going with a small lineup with Carl Tamayo playing the four and Quiambao taking the three spot.
Sotto also came alive in the second quarter before Tamayo nailed a triple to cut the Gilas deficit to just five, 39-44.
Gilas took a 51-46 lead but Jordan regained its footing and restored 58-54 lead.
Perez, however, took over in the final frame and spearheaded the offense for Gilas. He even had the shot to win it in regulation but missed it, sending the game to overtime.
Freddy Ybrahim paced the Falcons with 22 points while naturalized player Jalen Harris added 19.

articles.title: Uganda: World's 'youngest monarch' dies aged 34
articles.summary: Oyo Nyimba, once recognized as the world's youngest reigning monarch, has died in his mid-30s. As one of Uganda's traditional monarchs, he took the throne of the Tooro kingdom in 1995, aged just 3.

image.caption: Oyo was formally coronated and handed full power in Tooro on the occasion of his 18th birthday in April 2010, with President Yoweri Museveni in attendanceImage: Samuel Egadu/Photoshot/picture alliance

blocks.text: Oyo Nyimba, a Ugandan king of the traditional pre-colonial kingdom of Tooro, has died aged just 34, the prime minister of Tooro announced late on Thursday.

"It is with profound sadness and a heavy heart that I announce the passing of His Majesty Omukama of Tooro, King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV," Tooro's regional leader Calvin Armstrong Rwomiire Akiiki said on social media.
What is the role of traditional monarchs in Uganda?
Uganda is a republic, ruled by a parliament and a nominally-elected head of state, longstanding President Yoweri Museveni, who's been in power since 1986.

But the country retains several traditional monarchies that still preside over their kingdoms as they were constituted in the pre-colonial period. Their power is largely symbolic but they wield considerable cultural and social influence.

Although they were banned after independence from British colonial rule in 1962 by a republican president who said he wanted to unify the nascent country, Museveni reinstated the traditional monarchs in 1993.
Oyo Nyimba was arguably the most recognizable among them, not least because of his unusual story, taking the throne at the age of just 3 in 1995.

blocks.caption: Oyo Nyimba frequently took an interest in youth development and issues affecting younger people during his reignImage: Nicholas Kajoba/Photoshot/picture alliance

blocks.text: What did officials say about Oyo Nyimba's death?

Regional leader Akiiki said that the king had died late on Thursday, without giving a cause of death. He said an official statement with further details, including the funeral and mourning arrangements, would follow later.
He called on the people of Tooro to "remain united, calm and prayerful during this difficult time."
Akiiki also issued one surprising claim about the unmarried young king, who since a very young age had been seen as perhaps Uganda's most eligible bachelor.

"The continuity of the Crown is assured," he said. "His Majesty leaves behind a Prince as heir, whose identity will be formally revealed at the appropriate time, in accordance with the traditions and customs of the Tooro kingdom."
Ugandan opposition leader Bobi Wine also issued condolences online.
Oyo Nyimba's death triggered an outpouring of grief online and widespread national coverage in Uganda.

blocks.caption: The Queen Mother of Tooro Kingdom Best Kemigisa was often close by her son's side, particularly earlier in his reign. Here she was accompanying him to the Kabira International school in the capital Kampala in 2006. Image: Mike Odongkara/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Who was King Oyo Nyimba of Tooro?
Born on April 16, 1992, Oyo was the second-born child of the late Omukama Patrick David Matthew Kaboyo Olimi III and Queen Best Kemigisa Kaboyo, with two sisters.
He ascended to the throne of Tooro, an area in western Uganda near the border to Congo, in 1995 after his father's death.
His unusual status as a modern "boy king" led to considerable interest early in his reign, including from world leaders like former Libyan strongman Moammar Gadhafi, who repeatedly visited Tooro.
Oyo's mother was among his key advisers in his younger years, as was President Yoweri Museveni, who attended his coming-of-age 18th birthday party in 2010 in Fort Portal.
In 2025, the Guinness Book of World Records said he was still the youngest reigning monarch alive, its most recent renewal of the record.

He spent time in the UK at Winchester University to conclude his education. This time away from Uganda prompted a failed challenge to his position in 2015, when his cousin Prince David Kijanangoma declared himself the rightful king of Tooro, accusing Oyo of neglecting the region.

Oyo was known as a lover of sports, and a fan of London football club Arsenal. He took interest in causes including HIV prevention, environmental conservation, tourism and climate change, for instance when he embarked on a hiking expedition in the Rwenzori Mountains in 2022 to try to showcase Uganda's tourism potential and the risks of climate change.
Prior to the news of his death, a Ugandan government minister was quoted in local media as saying Oyo had been seriously ill and was seeking medical treatment in the US.

articles.title: Marcoleta calls Guteza recantation 'spurious,' cites alleged family threats
articles.summary: Senator Rodante Marcoleta on Friday denied conspiring with former Marine Orly Guteza, who recently recanted his earlier statement that he delivered suitcases of cash to former Speaker Ferdinand…

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 10:49pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

Senator Rodante Marcoleta on Friday denied conspiring with former Marine Orly Guteza, who recently recanted his earlier statement that he delivered suitcases of cash to former Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez in connection with the flood control scandal.

In a statement posted on Facebook through his administrator, Marcoleta described Guteza’s new affidavit as “spurious,” saying it “contains a narration of events that is both physically implausible and/or psychologically improbable.”

“It is improbable for me to conspire with Guteza, then a complete stranger to me. It is improbable for myself and Rep. Defensor to concoct a detailed account of the massive transport of money in luggages within one hour in a restaurant,” Marcoleta said.

“It is implausible that within a few minutes of my arrival at said restaurant and getting introduced to Guteza, I could have probed his character, developed complete trust and confidence in him, acquainted myself with the details of his narrative, re-wrote his account, instructed him on the succeeding steps, and then dashed back to the Senate,” he added.

Marcoleta, who is currently detained at the New Quezon City Jail on plunder charges, also alleged that threats to the life and liberty of Guteza’s wife and children forced the former Marine to change his statement.
Nevertheless, Marcoleta said Guteza’s recantation was “understandable” given his alleged circumstances.

“My respect for MSgt. Guteza has not been diminished by the release of his completely different statement on August 19, 2026. It was unsurprisingly expected as it was obviously understandable given the ordeal he was subjected to,” Marcoleta said.
Guteza had previously claimed that he personally delivered cash to the residences of former lawmaker Zaldy Co and Romualdez.
Following his testimony, Guteza disappeared from public view.

He later executed a new affidavit claiming that Marcoleta and former congressman Mike Defensor had tapped him to fabricate accusations against Romualdez in exchange for money and scholarships for his children.
Aside from Guteza, four other former security aides of Co have recanted statements linking Romualdez and other personalities to the alleged flood control scam.

Marcoleta further alleged that shortly after Guteza testified before the Senate Blue Ribbon Committee in September 2025, he was “virtually rendered incommunicado” and “held under the custody of persons only he can identify.”

“And then he was made to sign and read out in camera a different statement forcing him to deny knowledge of what he earlier testified and to accuse me and former Rep. Mike Defensor of orchestration upon ‘bribe’ of money,” he said.
According to Marcoleta, Guteza told his wife that the new statement “was not his,” but that he had to sign it “to spare his family from potential danger.”
“Finally, his wife admitted that indeed their family was being subjected to threats by the same persons restricting his movement and liberty,” he added.

Marcoleta maintained that Guteza’s testimony during the September 2025 hearing was a “detailed account of his personal knowledge of the plunderous acts” allegedly committed by Romualdez and several others.

“[T]he other statement attributed to Guteza only asserts a general denial, one which contains no evidentiary value (People v. Manlapaz, G.R. No. 254747, 13 July 2022), especially when compared to a detailed account of personal knowledge by the same witness,” Marcoleta said. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Egyptian queen’s 673-diamond necklace stolen in Vienna smash-and-grab raid
articles.summary:
Police hunt two suspects after historic 200-carat piece is snatched from Austrian museum during opening hours

Austrian police are hunting two men alleged to have stolen a 200-carat platinum…

blocks.text: Austrian police are hunting two men alleged to have stolen a 200-carat platinum necklace encrusted with 673 diamonds that was on loan to a museum in Vienna and once belonged to Egyptian royalty.

Authorities in the capital released pictures of the suspects captured by security cameras during the heist at the Museum of Applied Arts (MAK), amid a rash of spectacular smash-and-grab thefts from European cultural institutions.
The unmasked men bought tickets to the exhibition before shattering a glass display case with a hammer during opening hours on Thursday afternoon and making off with the diamond necklace.

blocks.caption: A visitor takes a picture of the platinum and diamond necklace, which dates from 1939 and belonged to Queen Nazli of Egypt, at the Pierres Précieuses exhibition in Paris. Photograph: Stéphane de Sakutin/AFP/Getty

blocks.text: In an appeal for information from the public, police said: “The perpetrators fled with the jewellery in an unknown direction.”

Officers fanned out through the city centre and deployed a police tracking dog to search for the suspects. The Kronen newspaper said investigators believed the men were probably carrying out a “contract job” on behalf of a criminal gang.

MAK said the piece had been snatched from a jewellery exhibition that had been on display since June, featuring more than 300 works by the French designers Van Cleef & Arpels. No one was hurt, although there were several witnesses in the room at the time.

Documentation for the show said the necklace once belonged to Queen Consort Nazli of Egypt, who wore it at the 1939 wedding of her daughter Fawzia to Iran’s then crown prince, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, who later became shah. The necklace was sold by Sotheby’s in New York in 2015 for $4.3m.

blocks.caption: Queen Nazli of Egypt, right, wearing the necklace at Princess Fawzia’s wedding in Cairo, 1939. Also pictured, from left, are: Queen Farida, King Farouk, Fawzia and Crown Prince Mohammad. Photograph: Bettmann Archive

blocks.text: The MAK said the exhibition brought together about 200 “unique and rarely seen objects” from its own collection and pieces spanning the 120-year history of the Parisian jewellery house, from the Van Cleef & Arpels patrimonial collection.
A guided tour planned for Friday afternoon was listed as “cancelled” on the museum website and the exhibition, which was due to end on 27 September, was temporarily closed.

European museums have been hit by a string of high-profile heists since thieves broke into the Louvre museum in Paris during the day last October and escaped within minutes with crown jewels worth €88m.
after newsletter promotion
In Spain on Thursday, thieves raided the Treasure of Villena, a collection of bronze age gold artefacts described as one of Europe’s most important prehistoric hoards.
This month, four of the most important works by the 15th-century Renaissance master Antonello da Messina were stolen during a national holiday from a museum in the Sicilian port city of Messina.

Two days earlier, Italian police said they had recovered three paintings by the French masters Paul Cézanne, Pierre-Auguste Renoir and Henri Matisse that were taken this year from a private museum near the northern city of Parma.

A report by Europol this month found that robberies at European museums are becoming increasingly violent, with thieves sometimes brandishing guns, assaulting staff and using sledgehammers, axes and even explosives to smash their way to targeted loot.

articles.title: Michael Poa has a lot more to say about DepEd confidential funds--House officials
articles.summary: Ranking congressmen believe lawyer Michael Poa can still reveal a lot of key details on the Department of Education's (DepEd) confidential fund use even after his 2024 House panel testimony. House…

blocks.text: Ranking congressmen believe lawyer Michael Poa can still reveal a lot of key details on the Department of Education's (DepEd) confidential fund use even after his 2024 House panel testimony.

House impeachment adviser Robert Ace Barbers and Deputy Speaker La Union 1st district Rep. Paolo Ortega V had this to say as they look forward to Poa's testimony next week in Vice President Sara Duterte's Senate impeachment trial.
Poa served as DepEd chief-of-staff and spokesperson during Vice President Duterte's tenure as education secretary. He is now part of Duterte’s defense team and serves as its spokesperson.
The House prosecution plans to call him as a hostile witness in connection with the alleged misuse of ₱112.5 million in DepEd confidential funds.

“Yung ating nasaksihan doon sa Committee on Good Government hearing, hindi pa siya yung complete, yung buong dapat itanong kay Attorney Michael Poa,” Barbers said Friday, Aug. 28 during an online press conference.
(What we witnessed at the Committee on Good Government hearing was not yet complete, not all of the questions that should be asked of Attorney Michael Poa.)

Barbers said Poa’s former position placed him close to documents and official responses that the senator-judges need to understand. “Gaya ni Ortonio, marami ring dokumentong dumadaan sa kanya na sinusuri nila at maaaring pinipirmahan nila. That must be made clear before the senator-judges."
(Like Ortonio, many documents also pass through him that they review and may sign.)
He was referring to Office of the Vice President (OVP) Assistant Chief-of-Staff Lemuel Ortonio, the previous hostile witness presented by the prosecution.
Ortega noted that Poa’s earlier House appearance came shortly after he resigned from DepEd, which limited the time available for questions.
But the impeachment court now offers the proper forum for a fuller examination.
“Nasa forum na siya ng impeachment court. Mas marami pong information at mas marami pong liwanag ang ma-shed niya sa mga topics na marami pong katanungan,” Ortega said.
(He is now in the forum of the impeachment court. He can provide more information and shed more light on the topics that have raised many questions.)

Official House accounts show Poa was involved in DepEd’s response to an Audit Observation Memorandum (AOM) concerning confidential funds. He also had a role in obtaining and submitting military certifications used in that response.

Two military officers, retired colonels Manaros Boransing II and Magtangol Panopio, previously told a House inquiry that they did not know the certifications would be used to support DepEd’s confidential fund liquidation.
Barbers said Poa’s legal training and senior role make his advice and actions relevant to the fund’s implementation.
“Yung paggamit nila nung pondong iyan, na confidential and intelligence fund na bihirang-bihirang ibigay sa DepEd secretary, tama ba ang pagkakagastos?” he asked.
(The use of that fund, which is a confidential and intelligence fund that is very rarely given to a DepEd secretary, was it spent properly?)
He said the impeachment court must establish what Poa reviewed, what he signed, what he knew about the documents, and what advice he gave to officials implementing the fund.
“Maraming tanong na dapat masagot, kaya I’m sure pinaghandaan ng prosecution iyan,” Barbers said.
(There are many questions that need to be answered, so I’m sure the prosecution has prepared for that.)
The twice-impeached Duterte served as DepEd chief from 2022 to 2024.

articles.title: Two-year curfew lifted in Sudan's capital
articles.summary: The military authorities retook control of the city 18 months ago, but the conflict continues elsewhere.

blocks.text: Sudan's military-led government has lifted a curfew and state of emergency in Khartoum imposed more than two years ago, state media says.

The authorities are taking this step 18 months after the army seized back control of the capital from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which it has been fighting in a civil war now in its fourth year.
But clashes continue in the south and west, with mounting evidence that the war is spilling across Sudan's borders.

More than two million of the roughly five million people who fled Khartoum after war erupted in April 2023 have returned to the city since fighting there ended in March 2025, according to the International Organization for Migration.
The aim of lifting the curfew is to help restore normal life to the capital.
The government has reopened the city's main airport for some flights and is encouraging businesses and embassies to come back.
But residents still struggle to rebuild their livelihoods.

Many have found widespread damage with many buildings looted. And they have to cope with constant power blackouts, due to alleged RSF drone attacks on electricity infrastructure and a lack of government funds to carry out repairs.

"The targeting of the electricity sector in particular was very significant," a spokesperson for the Khartoum state government, Altayeb Saadeldin, told the Reuters news agency, listing looting of copper wires and fuel and other components, as well as drone attacks, as reasons for the outages.
An RSF source responded that the allegations were "incorrect and army propaganda".

Despite lifting the state of emergency, the authorities remain wary of RSF infiltration. The Sudan News Agency said security patrols would continue operating across the state and locals traveling at night would need to carry identification documents.

Reports compiled by BBC Monitoring say the army continues to carry out security sweeps across greater Khartoum, targeting alleged RSF sleeper cells, undocumented foreigners and criminals involved in illegal activities.
In the meantime, there is growing concern that the war is drawing in neighbouring countries.

Chad is accusing the Sudanese army of carrying out an air strike that hit a military convoy in Ennedi-Est province, about 100km (62 miles) inside Chadian territory, on 20 August. It has reportedly put its forces along the border on maximum alert.
Sudan has rejected the charge, saying it is surprised that its army was blamed without an independent investigation.

In a statement, the foreign ministry said it "affirms that the Sudanese army fulfils its constitutional duty to defend Sudan's sovereignty, security and territorial integrity, and to confront the threats facing the country, while remaining committed to respecting the sovereignty of neighbouring states and refraining from targeting their territories".
Sudan accuses Chad of permitting the passage of RSF military supplies delivered by the United Arab Emirates (UAE) through its airports and border crossings.
The UAE and Chad deny the allegations despite similar findings by UN experts and investigative reports by international media.

The attack on the Chadian convoy prompted the US Senior Adviser for Arab and African Affairs, Massad Boulos to express "deep concern" about the risk of Sudan's war threatening regional peace and stability.

Boulos has been urging the parties to immediately accept a humanitarian truce. He has grown increasingly frustrated with the Sudanese military, which refuses to engage in a peace process unless the RSF disarms and withdraws from the territory it has occupied.

"The United States condemns the SAF's recent air strikes inside Chad," Boulos wrote in a post on X. "There is no military solution to this conflict - and absolutely no justification for expanding the violence beyond Sudan's borders.
"External financial and military support to the warring parties must stop," he added.

This month the US envoy presented a draft resolution to the UN Security Council that would extend a 2005 weapons embargo on Darfur - the stronghold of the RSF - across the entire country and include a ban on attack drones, which are increasingly used by both sides.

Sudan's government and army have rejected the proposal. According to local media reports officials argue that this unfairly equates the recognised national military with a paramilitary force and restricts its ability to defend citizens against an insurgency.
