articles.summary: The value of the country’s metallic mineral production from January to June rose by more than 40 percent to over ₱200 billion compared to a year ago, driven by higher gold prices that offset weaker…

blocks.text: The value of the country’s metallic mineral production from January to June rose by more than 40 percent to over ₱200 billion compared to a year ago, driven by higher gold prices that offset weaker production volume.
Data from the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) showed that the country's total mineral output reached ₱202.18 billion in the first half, higher than last year’s ₱142.99 billion.
Gold stood as the country’s most prized mineral asset by the end of June, accounting for nearly 57 percent of the total value.
The value of gold output during the reference period surged by 42 percent to ₱114.50 billion from ₱80.43 billion, based on MGB data.

The increase in value was fueled by higher prices for the mineral, which averaged $4,512 per troy ounce in the second quarter, up by 37 percent from $3,293 per troy ounce in the same period last year, based on commodity price data from the World Bank.
The elevated gold prices helped counter the over 12 percent drop in production to 12,771 kilos by the end of June from 14,604 kilos.
Meanwhile, the country’s output of nickel direct shipping ore in the first half increased by a quarter to 19.24 million dry metric tons (DMT) from 15.32 million DMT.
The value of nickel direct shipping ore amounted to ₱42.18 billion, an improvement of 47.5 percent from ₱28.59 billion.
MGB data also showed that the production of mixed nickel-cobalt sulfide went up by more than half to ₱27.96 billion from ₱18.02 billion.
Meanwhile, copper concentrate output climbed by one percent to ₱13.85 billion from ₱13.67 billion in the previous year, as the volume of the mineral remained relatively stable at around 120,000 DMT.

Silver production, on the other hand, ballooned by 77 percent to ₱2.48 billion by the end of June from ₱1.4 billion. This was despite its production volume dropping by 23 percent to 18,607 kilos from 24,091 kilos.

The government is expecting the country’s mineral industry to become more productive in the coming years following the issuance of Executive Order (EO) No. 122, which establishes an integrated national framework to develop the critical minerals industry.
Mining groups expect the policy to create a predictable environment that would encourage the entry of long-term investments in exploration, mine development, and mineral processing.
At present, the government said there are still around nine million hectares of prospective areas across the country that have the potential to host critical mineral resources.

articles.title: Ombudsman files malversation complaint vs. Zaldy Co over Bulacan 'ghost' project
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman has filed a malversation complaint against former Ako Bicol Party-list Rep. Zaldy Co and other officials of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) over a…

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 10:03pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

The Office of the Ombudsman has filed a malversation complaint against former Ako Bicol Party-list Rep. Zaldy Co and other officials of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) over a Bulacan ghost flood control project.
In a statement on Friday, the Ombudsman said the project amounted to P77 million—but was never built.
“The project supposedly started last February 24, 2025 and was declared to be 100% accomplished on May 2, 2025. However, upon inspection, it was non-existent,” the ruling said.

Therefore, the Ombudsman said there was probably cause to charge Co, Henry Alcantara, Brice Ericson Diaz Hernandez, Arjay Salvador Domasig, Jaypee De Leon Mendoza, Niño Lawrence Vergara Morales, Juanito Coronel Mendoza, Floralyn Yutuc Simbulan and Christina Mae Del Rosario Pineda with one count each of Malversation of Public Funds through Falsification of Public Documents.
Co is currently outside the country, having been spotted multiple times across Europe.
John Paul Estrada and Mark Tecsay, staff members of Co, were also indicted.
However, Alcantara was not included in the filing of information since he was admitted to the witness protection program.
The Bulacan case focuses on the construction of a riverbank protection structure along the Balagtas River in Purok 4, Barangay San Juan in Balagtas.
The project was awarded to SYMS Construction Trading, which is owned by Sally Santos.
The Ombudsman noted that there was repeated approval of payment to SYMS despite irregularities in the Monthly Certificates of Payment and Statements of Work Accomplished.
This is a “strong indication of their participation in the devious schemes of misappropriating the funds for flood control projects,” the Ombudsman resolution said.

The Office said that Alcantara had collected the kickbacks and delivered them to Co, who ensured that the project would be inserted in the National Expenditure Program and passed in the General Appropriations Act.
There was also a repeated failure by those involved to review, inspect and certify the projects. This could not be treated as ordinary mistakes, the Ombudsman said.

“Here, respondents acted with evident bad faith and/or gross inexcusable negligence when they issued the pertinent documents and certifications that led to the diversion of public funds… for a project that turned out to be non-existent or incomplete. The repeated failure to exercise due diligence is very telling,” the resolution stated.

Meanwhile, the Ombudsman dismissed for lack of probable cause the charges of violating section 3 of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act against Co, Alcantara, Estrada and Tecsay. This section pertains to the direct or indirect request for gifts.
Alcantara was also not included in the aforementioned charge because he is a state witness. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Africa's aging autocrats fight to stay in power
articles.summary: As some of Africa's longest-serving leaders grow older, they are using different tactics to extend their rule. But age, succession battles and public pressure pose new challenges.

image.caption: Backed by a loyal inner circle, Paul Biya (center) was sworn in for an eighth term as president of Cameroon in November 2025Image: Angel Ngwe/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Power can be seductive, and many who possess it want to hold on for as long as possible. The leaders of China and Russia, for example, cleared the way for additional terms years ago, and in the United States, the president occasionally speaks of another run for office, even though the US Constitution does not allow it.
From the perspective of Paul Biya, however, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump are still relatively new to office.
Cameroon's president has been head of state since 1982. In 2025, Biya began his eighth term — which is officially due to end on November 6, 2032, just a few months before his 100th birthday.
The 93-year-old has given no official indication that he intends to step down, and the position of vice president remains vacant.
Paul Biya in Cameroon: A loyal leadership circle with one weak spot
During his 44 years in office, Biya has built a stable network of loyal allies that keeps the machinery of government running despite his lengthy absences.

The 93-year-old has now spent two and a half months in Geneva, Switzerland, continuing to issue decrees and make personnel decisions from abroad. In mid-June, his spokesperson denied rumors Biya was receiving treatment in a hospital and stated that the president was in good health.
"There is continuity, but that also means there is little momentum for reform within the government,” Beverly Ochieng, senior analyst at consultancy Global Risk, told DW.

And while Biya's power apparatus has helped cushion the impact of the president's long absence, that does not necessarily mean the most influential figures on the ground are united. After all, a post-Biya era is now in sight, and several of his allies are rumored to have ambitions of succeeding him.
Who's to blame for Cameroon's woes?

"When everyone is lining up to potentially succeed Biya, it also means that the elites may begin challenging one another," Ochieng said. Such rivalry, she warned, could lead to major disruptions, including the possibility of a military coup.
Analyst Levi Mboushou recently voiced similar concerns on DW's AfricaLink podcast.

"Everyone feels the fear and uncertainty, but no one dares to look directly at it because we all have to deal with this repressive regime. You see something, but you say nothing. That is the situation in Cameroon at the moment," he said.
Yoweri Museveni in Uganda: Signs of a dynasty?
Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni is only slightly younger, both in age and years in office.

The 81-year-old has been president since 1986 and, like Biya, recently embarked on another term. His succession also remains unresolved, although his son, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has recently attracted considerable attention as head of the military.
According to Ochieng, the dynamics in Uganda are complex, not least because military elites and the ruling National Resistance Movement (NRM) have their own internal power structures.

blocks.caption: Is Muhoozi Kainerugaba (center, seen here in 2019) being groomed to eventually succeed his father?Image: Joseph Kiggundu/Photoshot/picture alliance

blocks.text: "Muhoozi has become the most visible figure primarily because he has a strong personality and enjoys the discreet backing of his father. His rise is not the result of support from either the NRM or the military leadership," she said.
Kainerugaba is increasingly emerging as a political figure, including on issues beyond military affairs.

In early July, he ordered the closure of several media outlets. At the time, a source from an international foundation who requested anonymity told DW: "We are witnessing a transfer of power to the president's son."
A similar development has been unfolding for years in Equatorial Guinea, where Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, who has ruled since 1979, appears to be gradually transferring power to his son.
Known by the nickname "Teodorin," he has served as first vice president since 2016 and now also controls the military.

In June, Teodorin announced the resignation of the entire government on behalf of his father. Observers interpreted the move as a sign that he is gradually becoming the public face of state authority.
Whether Museveni will actually arrange his succession during his lifetime remains uncertain.
Ochieng believes that, in the event of a sudden power vacuum, Uganda could either hold constitutionally mandated elections or follow a scenario similar to that seen in Chad in 2021.
Then-President Idriss Deby was killed in clashes with rebels. The constitution was suspended, allowing his son, Mahamat Idriss Deby Itno, to take power.
Emmerson Mnangagwa in Zimbabwe: Party before people
Zimbabwe also amended its constitution this year, making it far less likely that President Emmerson Mnangagwa could be voted out of office.

In June, both chambers of parliament approved changes extending the terms of parliament and the president from five to seven years. Even more fundamentally, the president will no longer be elected directly by the people but by parliament, where the ruling ZANU-PF party enjoys comfortable majorities.

In July, the 83-year-old Mnangagwa signed the amended constitution into law. However, the opposition and some constitutional experts argue that a referendum should still be held. The government, by contrast, considers the constitutional amendment process complete.

blocks.caption: Emmerson 'Ed' Mnangagwa campaigned for reelection with giant billboards in 2023Image: Siphiwe Sibeko/REUTERS

blocks.text: "We are not surprised," Chiedza Mlingwa, deputy spokesperson for the Constitution Defenders Forum, said at the time on DW's AfricaLink podcast.

"The only thing one could be surprised by is the audacity, nothing else. We have observed this pattern since independence in 1980: ZANU-PF works to stay in power. The party does not believe in relinquishing power."
Ochieng noted that countries such as Togo and Cote d'Ivoire have also implemented constitutional changes aimed at preserving power in recent years.

Meanwhile, in Senegal, a constitutional amendment is being discussed amid tensions between former allies at the top of the state, President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and Speaker of Parliament Ousmane Sonko, both of whom are significantly younger than the continent's other long-ruling leaders.

"Even when legal safeguards exist, if they are not designed in a way that guarantees citizen participation, public debate, civil society engagement, or oversight by other institutions, then it becomes possible for unilateral decisions to be made at the highest levels of government," said Ochieng.
The weakening of institutions to allow individuals to remain in power, she added, is not an African problem but a global one.
Lucy Riley contributed to this article.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: French far-right leader Jordan Bardella to address Reform UK party conference
articles.summary:
Speech part of effort to strengthen National Rally party’s international ties before Marine Le Pen’s presidential bid

The French far-right leader

blocks.text: The French far-right leader Jordan Bardella is to give a speech at Reform UK’s party conference in Birmingham next week as he attempts to boost international ties before Marine Le Pen’s bid for the French presidency next spring.
Le Pen’s far-right, anti-immigration National Rally (RN) is high in the polls and she is predicted to reach the final round of the French presidential race in May.

Le Pen launched her presidential campaign this summer despite a Paris appeal court upholding her conviction for being at the centre of the embezzlement of more than €2.8m (£2.4m) in European parliament funds and funnelling the money into her party between 2004 and 2016. She has appealed against the ruling to France’s highest court.

Le Pen, the RN’s parliamentary leader in the National Assembly and the party leader from 2011 to 2021, has said she will run for president on a joint ticket with Bardella as prime minister. Under the French political system, the president, who is head of state and has authority on foreign policy and national security, directly appoints a prime minister as head of government to run domestic affairs.
Bardella’s team confirmed that he would travel to Birmingham to address the Reform UK conference next Friday and hold a joint press conference with the Reform leader, Nigel Farage.

blocks.caption: Marine Le Pen has said she will run for president on a joint ticket with Jordan Bardella as prime minister.  Photograph: Yoan Valat/EPA

blocks.text: Bardella, 30, and Farage, 62, held a private lunch in London at the end of last year, where they discussed anti-immigration policy.

“Nigel Farage is a great patriot, he has fought all his life to defend his country’s independence, freedom and sovereignty,” Bardella said after his talks with Farage. He said he hoped the Reform leader would be Britain’s next prime minister.

Bardella said: “We could perhaps tomorrow be at the head of our respective governments, in a situation where he would be leading a British government and me at the head of a French government. So we’re preparing our future cooperation.

“I think that we share a joint determination to stop immigration – to protect our countries from a wave of immigration to Europe that is just beginning. We’re conscious that our people want to protect their identity, and I think we can find extremely pragmatic and extremely firm solutions to control immigration together.”
after newsletter promotion

Bardella, who is a member of the European parliament and president of RN, has supported tighter police cooperation between London and Paris on people crossing the Channel on small boats but wanted migrants returned to their countries of origin, not to France.

blocks.caption: Marine Le Pen and Nigel Farage have clashed in the past, Farage rejecting a suggestion from Le Pen that Ukip could join a European parliament coalition with the Front National.   Photograph: Global Radio/PA

blocks.text: Le Pen has had a thorny relationship with Farage. In 2014, when he was the Ukip leader and her party was still called Front National (FN), they were competing to be seen as the EU’s leading Eurosceptics in European parliament elections. That year, Farage rejected a suggestion from Le Pen that Ukip could join a European parliament coalition with the FN, saying there was “prejudice and antisemitism” in Le Pen’s party. She rejected his comments, saying Farage had made “defamatory” and “extremely disagreeable declarations” in an attempt to boost his popularity.

The Reform UK leader was recently re-elected in a byelection in Clacton. However, parliament’s standards commissioner immediately reopened an investigation into whether he should have declared a series of gifts provided to him shortly before the last general election. These include a £5m personal gift from the crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne, first revealed by the Guardian, and further financial support from his friend and convicted fraudster George Cottrell.

articles.title: Rains batter parts of Luzon as Habagat strengthens
articles.summary: Several parts of Luzon on Friday were battered by heavy rains brought by the enhanced Southwest Monsoon (Habagat).

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 9:54pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
Several parts of Luzon on Friday were battered by heavy rains brought by the enhanced Southwest Monsoon (Habagat).
In a “24 Oras” report by Tina Panganiban-Perez, a house in San Marcelino, Zambales could be seen slowly giving way under the force of strong floodwaters.
The residents were able to evacuate before the house collapsed.
Also in San Marcelino, authorities had to temporarily suspend relief operations after floodwaters overtook a road.
RAINFALL ALERT: Red in Bataan, Zambales, Pampanga, parts of Bulacan (Saturday, 5 a.m.)
RAINFALL ALERT: Red in Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga, parts of Tarlac and Bulacan (Saturday, 2 a.m.)
LIVE UPDATES: Habagat rains affect parts of PH on Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026
The national highway in Cabangan, Zambales was also submerged, making it difficult for vehicles to pass.
Meanwhile, the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office of Occidental Mindoro recommended declaring a state of calamity in the province. Damage was estimated at more than P2 billion.
After briefly weakening, the Southwest Monsoon intensified again amid a low pressure area east northeast of Itbayat, Batanes.
The first weeks of August saw persistent monsoon rains that triggered widespread flooding and landslides.
Together with cyclones Luis and Maymay, the Southwest Monsoon has killed at least 31 people. —Jean Mangaluz/VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Oslo mayor calls off wedding ceremony after death of Norway's king
articles.summary: Anne Lindboe, the mayor of Norway's capital, had planned to marry her fiance on Friday.

blocks.text: Oslo mayor calls off wedding ceremony after death of Norway's king
Image source, Getty Images
The Mayor of Oslo, Anne Lindboe, has been engaged for five years
Oslo's Mayor Anne Lindboe has called off her wedding ceremony because of the death of King Harald V of Norway.
The wedding with her fiancé Pål Sandvid was planned to take place on Friday but was postponed after the king died earlier the same day, her political adviser confirmed to the BBC.
"It's hard to imagine an Oslo and a Norway without you. You didn't need a crown to be king," Lindboe wrote in a tribute to the late monarch on Instagram.
Harald reigned for 35 years and died at the national hospital in Norway's capital, where he was being treated for a rare blood condition. His son, King Haakon VIII, ascended the throne on Friday.
"Even the majority of Norwegians who never met you in person still felt like they knew you," Lindboe added in her tribute.
No new date has been set for the wedding yet, Lindboe's political adviser said.
After five years together, Lindboe announced the couple's engagement in June this year.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Oslo's mayor pictured next to King Harald V of Norway in March 2025

blocks.text: Oslo's mayor pictured next to King Harald V of Norway in March 2025
The late king was a popular and reforming leader in Norway who modernised the monarchy.
He broke with tradition by marrying a commoner, Queen Sonja, and served as a unifying figure during Norway's most difficult moments.
Harald died a day before their 58th wedding anniversary.
Members of the public have been gathering to lay flowers at a memorial outside the Royal Palace in Oslo.
Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said in a televised memorial address that his country was "united in grief and gratitude" for Harald's service and that his "legacy lives on".
The UK's King Charles III said he was mourning his "dear cousin". King Harald V was a second cousin of the King's mother, Queen Elizabeth II.
Haakon VIII is the great-great-great-grandson of Queen Victoria.

articles.title: DOH investigates child deaths after measles-rubella vaccination Phase 3
articles.summary: The Department of Health (DOH) is investigating the reported deaths of children following the implementation of Phase 3 of the Measles-Rubella Supplemental Immunization Activity (MR-SIA).

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 9:50pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
The Department of Health (DOH) is investigating the reported deaths of children following the implementation of Phase 3 of the Measles-Rubella Supplemental Immunization Activity (MR-SIA).
In a statement, the DOH expressed its condolences to the loved ones of the children and assured the public that it was closely monitoring the cases.
The agency said it was coordinating with local government units and other government agencies to conduct a thorough investigation.
"Nakikipag-ugnayan ang DOH sa mga lokal na pamahalaan at iba pang ahensya para sa masusing imbestigasyon sa mga naiulat na kaso," the DOH said.
(The DOH is coordinating with local government units and other agencies to conduct a thorough investigation into the reported cases.)

As part of the investigation into Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI), the DOH said experts are reviewing the children's clinical records, vaccination history, laboratory test results, and other relevant information to determine the possible cause of each case.
"Binibigyang-diin ng DOH na ang hindi pangkaraniwang pangyayaring naganap matapos ang pagbabakuna ay hindi awtomatikong sanhi ng bakuna," the DOH said.
"Kailangan munang dumaan ang mga ganitong kaso sa masusing pagsusuri at imbestigasyon ng mga eksperto upang matukoy kung may kaugnayan sa pagbabakuna o kung may iba pang posibleng sanhi," it added.
"Hinihikayat ang publiko na iwasang gumawa ng mga konklusyon o magbahagi ng mga hindi beripikadong impormasyon habang nagpapatuloy ang imbestigasyon," the DOH said.
"Nanatiling ligtas at epektibo ang mga bakuna laban sa mga sakit na maaaring maiwasan sa pamamagitan ng pagbabakuna, kabilang ang tigdas at rubella," it added.

(The DOH emphasizes that an unusual event occurring after vaccination does not automatically mean that it was caused by the vaccine. Such cases must first undergo thorough assessment and investigation by experts to determine whether they are related to the vaccination or whether there are other possible causes. The public is urged to refrain from drawing conclusions or sharing unverified information while the investigation is ongoing. Vaccines remain safe and effective against vaccine-preventable diseases, including measles and rubella. —NB, GMA News

articles.title: What the CIA director’s mystery trip to Moscow says about Putin's next move
articles.summary: An unannounced but highly visible flight to Moscow by CIA Director John Ratcliffe aboard a U.S. Air Force transport plane this week has ignited a fierce debate over Vladimir Putin’s next military…

image.caption: Russian President Vladimir Putin attends a meeting at the Kremlin in Moscow on Aug. 26, 2026. (Sputnik/Mikhail Metzel)

blocks.text: As Russia’s war against Ukraine reaches an inflection point, a conspicuous U.S. intelligence mission to Moscow this week has revealed a fractured debate among allies over Vladimir Putin’s next move.

For weeks now, analysts have speculated that Russia’s strongman president has given up on the notion that U.S. President Donald Trump might be able to coerce Ukraine into meeting his maximalist surrender terms. The thinking is Putin may have decided his five-year war against the country can only be concluded by expanding the conflict.
With Russia’s economy worsening and the pool of volunteers willing to accept a generous paycheque to fight in Ukraine dwindling, Putin could be facing several options.

Ukrainian intelligence officials believe he will soon initiate an unpopular mass mobilization that could send hundreds of thousands of new conscripts into battle, with the goal of overwhelming Ukraine's overstretched defences.
Soldiers from Russia’s poorer regions have made up a disproportionate amount of the fighting force in Ukraine. A country-wide mobilization could draw in men from the more affluent major cities.

Military think-tanks on both sides of the Atlantic have also warned Putin could try to divide Ukraine’s backers in NATO by staging some kind of provocation in Eastern Europe aimed at splitting the alliance.
Carney says Putin's 'barbarism' against Ukraine will not succeed

Presumed and confirmed Russia hybrid attacks across Europe — including attempted assassinations, sabotage and frequent drone incursions — have all intensified of late. But planners remain concerned that Russia could be tempted to seize a slice of Russian-speaking territory in a neighbouring country as a test to see how the alliance would respond.
Russian officials themselves have raised the possibility this week that they could strike directly at Western weapons manufacturers who supply Ukraine, most notably in Great Britain.
Mystery visit
The speculation over Putin’s next move hit a fever pitch earlier this week after the unusual visit by CIA Director John Ratcliffe to Russia.

Rather than slipping into Moscow on a business jet, the standard protocol for clandestine diplomacy, Ratcliffe arrived at Vnukovo airport aboard a massive, highly visible U.S. Air Force C-17 Globemaster.
Its transponder broadcast the flight path openly across the Atlantic.
U.S. officials appeared to want the world to know Ratcliffe’s visit to Moscow was significant and that they had something they wanted the Russians to hear clearly.

"It kind of reached a point inside the administration where they said, ‘We need to read the Russians the riot act,'" said Glen Howard with the Saratoga Foundation, a Washington, D.C.-based security think-tank with a focus on Ukraine.
But what message was Ratcliffe trying to convey?

Initially, the Wall Street Journal reported the mission was a direct ultimatum to Putin: Back off an escalating grey-zone campaign of hybrid sabotage against NATO's eastern flank or risk triggering a direct allied response.

Military planners have long contemplated whether Putin, in order to get a favourable settlement in Ukraine, might try to draw the United States or NATO directly into the war. Staging a modest attack on a small Baltic nation and testing the Article 5 collective defence provision of the NATO treaty might be one way to do that.
The following day, however, Trump himself appeared to dismiss this, saying he wasn’t worried about a Russian attack on NATO, calling Radcliffe’s trip "semi-routine."

Hours later, the New York Times published an account along the lines of what Trump said that contradicted the earlier reporting. It suggested NATO was not the main topic of the meeting; instead, the warning was for Putin to end his war on Ukraine before Russia’s economic and military situation worsened.
Canada at the front
Canada’s largest overseas military deployment is in the Baltics. More than 2,000 soldiers are based in Latvia, tasked with the goal of deterring any Russian adventurism there.
Canadian military and security analyst Wesley Wark doesn’t believe Putin is interested in provoking NATO directly, even with the U.S. politically and militarily weakened by the war in Iran.

"I think concerns about Article 5 are overblown," Wark told CBC News in an email. "My main guess is that Ratcliffe went to Moscow to deliver a message primarily about the seriousness with which the U.S. intends to mount economic sanctions against Iran, with a warning to Russia not to interfere."
Russia is one of Iran’s key international military backers and Putin’s government may be giving Iran targeting information to help guide strikes on U.S. military bases in the Persian Gulf.

The immediate reaction to Ratcliffe's visit from countries such as Latvia also downplayed the risk of a confrontation with NATO. The country’s foreign minister posted on social media that "Latvia’s threat assessment remains unchanged."

Yet in Britain — where Putin’s agents have notoriously staged attacks before, including the deadly 2018 Novichok attack in Salisbury — intelligence agencies have warned that sensitive industries in the defence sector should be on high alert.

On Wednesday, Russian foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova was unusually direct with her threats, warning that Russia could strike at targets inside and outside the U.K. if the British government didn’t back off on its assistance to Ukraine.
On his recent visit to Kyiv, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he would give Ukrainians the blueprints to make their own long-range missiles that could hit targets deep inside Russia.
Onslaught against Ukraine

Ukrainian authorities appear convinced the potential Russian threats against NATO, Great Britain and other targets in Europe are just distractions, and that when Putin’s escalation comes, it will be directed almost entirely at them.

"I think Putin sees a window of opportunity," said Yuriy Boyechko, who runs the U.S.-based Hope for Ukraine, a humanitarian organization that sends emergency supplies to the country in the aftermath of Russian bombing.

"I think Putin is planning this winter to basically bring Ukrainian society to pain and despair, because of lack of energy or the lack of food ... and they [Ukrainians] will turn on the Ukrainian government."
While Putin's plan stands to bring immense hardship to Ukraine in the coming months, he says it won't break the country's spirit.
"As we know from the past, none of his strategies are successful. So I'm optimistic about that."
The ferocity and intensity of missile attacks on the capital, Kyiv, and other cities has escalated of late, with as many as 800 Russian drones being launched on a single night.
The scarcity of interceptor missiles, such as U.S.-made Patriots, has left cities defenceless and sent civilian casualties soaring.
Boyechko says as Ukrainian cities are being terrorized, he believes Putin will use his newly mobilized army of recruits to try to overwhelm the country’s defences in the south.

"His hope is that those 600,000 new troops will be able to break through the front lines and capture some territories. He is not looking just to take Donetsk, Luhansk region or Zaporizhzhia — he wants to go all the way to Kyiv."
Risky mobilization

Putin reportedly believed the invasion he launched in February 2022 would only last a few days and that Kyiv would fall easily. Instead, Western sources claim Russia has suffered up to 1.4 million casualties, including those killed, wounded or missing.

A mass mobilization carries risks for Putin, too, says Howard of Saratoga. It will be immensely unpopular and could spark a new brain-drain from the country. Civilian factories and agriculture could also be robbed of workers required to maintain basic supply chains and keep Russia’s wartime economy going.
"What he may do is in increments try to generate the forces," Howard said.

Whether Ratcliffe’s recent flight was meant to shore up NATO, protect the Baltics or isolate Iran, the grim reality on the ground suggests Ukraine will bear the immediate brunt of whatever direction Putin chooses.

articles.title: Shootings surge as drug gangs torment Brussels
articles.summary: This year alone there have been more than 65 shootings in the Belgian capital, as drug crime soars.

blocks.text: Image source, EPA
ByBruno Boelpaep
Reporting fromBrussels
Last Monday night, drug gangs turned Salvatore's pizzeria in Brussels into a crime scene.
"We dropped to the floor. I had clients eating on the terrace with children. Look, we can see the bullet impacts everywhere."
His restaurant sits on a pretty little square in St Gilles. It's a central area of the city, close to the international Midi train station, where passengers arrive on trains from London and Paris.
Shootings related to drug trafficking have become routine in the Belgian capital over the past couple of years. There were over 100 in 2025 alone, and more than 65 shootings so far this year.
This was the third shooting in this neighbourhood in just three days.
"Are we in an American gangster movie? This needs to stop," Salvatore says.

blocks.caption: Image caption, "Are we in an American gangster movie? This needs to stop," says Salvatore, after a shooting at his Brussels pizzeria

blocks.text: "Are we in an American gangster movie? This needs to stop," says Salvatore, after a shooting at his Brussels pizzeria
A suspected drug dealer was shot in the leg in the same area the day before.
Now Murielle and her dog Chéva are sitting at that exact spot, just across the street: "We can still see the trace of the pool of blood."
Murielle is 70, and hopes peace soon returns to her street.
"I like it here. It's like a little village inside the city. Even the drug dealers used to be polite and decent. I would just tell them to go further away and they'd say, 'Yes, ok mama!'"

blocks.caption: Image caption, Murielle says the drug dealers used to be polite in this part of the city - but not any more

blocks.text: Murielle says the drug dealers used to be polite in this part of the city - but not any more
Drug dealing is happening in plain sight here. Only five minutes after I arrive, I witness a transaction.
A buyer walks up to the seller, shakes their hand, and walks away with the drugs. Crack has become widely consumed amongst the poorest in this area of Brussels.
"Things have changed in the past six months," says Murielle. "The business has intensified. Sometimes you even see consumers queuing to buy drugs. And now gangs are fighting over this spot."
A successful drug-dealing point in Brussels nets up to €50,000 ($58,000; £43,000) per day or more for the dealer, according to the chief of Brussels South Police, Jurgen de Landsheer.
Organised crime in the Belgian capital has become significantly more violent, he says.
At the heart of it all is money. There are more than 200 drug-dealing points across the city, according to the police.
The rise of drug-related violence in the Belgian capital echoes the situation of other European cities such as the French port of Marseille.

Cocaine has become widely available in Europe, the continent's ports serving as entry points for the drug. The port of Antwerp, just 40km (25 miles) away, has seen record cocaine seizures in recent years.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Antwerp has seen record seizures on drugs in recent years

blocks.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images
Antwerp has seen record seizures on drugs in recent years
Jurgen de Landsheer says gangs in Brussels are now adopting methods seen in Marseille, although he insists his city has not reached the same level of violence.

"We don't have no-go zones here in Brussels. It's not easy to go in some neighbourhoods, but we go everywhere. We don't want to become like some neighbourhoods in Marseille, so we'll do everything to stop it."
A police station even came under attack last weekend.
CCTV footage shows two men on a scooter stopping in front of the building and shooting at the door several times with what looks like an AK-47 before leaving on their scooter.
This marks an escalation, as it is the first time criminals have targeted police. Usually, the shootings involve rival gangs.

"We see a lot of young people getting paid a few hundred euros. They get a weapon, AK-47 or other heavy weapon, and then they get a mission. To shoot a person in the leg, for example, or to try to kill somebody. And they get very little money for this."
De Landsheer says some of the people his men arrest are as young as 12, and that makes it very dangerous for the whole community.
"The biggest danger is a stray bullet."

blocks.caption: Chief of Brussels South Police, Jurgen de Landsheer stands in a blue shirt on a rooftop in Brussels

blocks.text: BBC
There is no magic solution. We need prevention over repression

blocks.caption: "There is no magic solution. We need prevention over repression", Source: Jurgen de Landsheer, Source description: Chief of Brussels South Police, Image: Chief of Brussels South Police, Jurgen de Landsheer stands in a blue shirt on a rooftop in Brussels

blocks.text: The spike in shootings has forced Belgian authorities to react and, on Thursday, Belgium's interior minister announced that an extra 40 police officers would be deployed in the problem area.
Jurgen de Landsheer is aware that police alone will not solve this crisis.

"There is no magic solution. We need prevention over repression. We can do our part and be present in the street, but our society also needs to give a future to the young people, do something with them. That's the social part."
Back in St Gilles, Salvatore says it's time for the violence to end.
"Nobody sleeps here at the moment. People talk about moving out, houses are losing value."
Murielle wants to believe that the worst is now behind.
"We will not be intimidated. We'll carry on living and we'll keep on protecting our lovely neighbourhood."

articles.title: Diokno: Sub judice rule should apply to all
articles.summary: Rule 18 of the Impeachment rules, which bars parties to the case from commenting on the merits of the impeachment case of Vice President Sara Duterte, or the sub judice rule, should be strictly…

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 9:37pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

Rule 18 of the Impeachment rules, which bars parties to the case from commenting on the merits of the impeachment case of Vice President Sara Duterte, or the sub judice rule, should be strictly imposed on all parties, including the Vice President, House prosecutor Chel Diokno of Akbayan party-list said Friday.

Diokno was referring to the sub judice rule, which states that the presiding officer, the members of the Senate, shall refrain from making any comments and disclosures in public about the merits of a pending impeachment trial” and that “the same shall likewise apply to the prosecutors, the person impeached, and their respective counsel and witnesses.”

“Well, para sa akin po ay walang silbi ang rules kung hindi naman siya mag-a-apply sa lahat, lalo na yung mga na directly involved sa case. Even if it is not under the impeachment rules, it's already covered by the Rules of Court,” Diokno said in a Super Radyo DZBB interview.
(That rule won’t have purpose if it won’t apply to all, especially those directly involved in the case.)

While Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero was reading the ruling, warning the parties to strictly observe the sub judice rule or face P30,000 for each offense and other sanctions, the Vice President issued a remark.

“A strong case does not need the adornment of theatrics. A senator calling a witness 'stupid,' a lawyer calling me the 'mastermind of a scam' or another witness referring to me as a 'brat' does not prove a case, nor does it produce evidence," she said.
Diokno then cited that comments on and off the court can both be sanctioned.

“You will be cited in direct contempt if you showed improper decorum or violated Rules of Court inside the courtroom, but if you are outside the court and you made a statement or wrote a column intended to influence the outcome of the case, that is indirect contempt,” Diokno said.
Diokno, however, clarified that not all statements on a pending case are contemptible or should be censured.

“The ruling of the impeachment court and a Supreme Court ruling on that matter are similar. It is covered under freedom of speech as long as there is no clear and present danger to the administration of justice,” Diokno said.

In a separate press conference, House prosecution panel adviser and spokesperson Robert Ace Barbers said the prosecution is considering adding more designated spokespersons to keep the Filipino public properly informed about the trial of Vice President Duterte in compliance with the sub judice rule.
“The more speakers, the more spokespersons, the better,” Barbers said.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Ombudsman: Bernardo's allegations linking Bersamins, Olaivar need more evidence
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman on Friday said that the government"s case against Executive Secretary Lucas Bersamin, his relative and former Undersecretary Adrian Bersamin of the Presidential…

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 9:27pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

The Office of the Ombudsman on Friday said that the government’s case against Executive Secretary Lucas Bersamin, his relative and former Undersecretary Adrian Bersamin of the Presidential Legislative Liaison Office, and Education Undersecretary Trygve Olaivar, whom state witness Roberto Bernardo accused of being involved in illegal budget insertions and kickbacks, would need more corroborating evidence.
Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano noted that while Bernardo is a credible witness, gathering evidence against these individuals is tough.

“They (Bersamins, OIaivar) are included in the second case, which the Ombudsman already described as a grand conspiracy to defraud the 2025 budget. So, in that sense, that case is still in fact finding, and we are sifting through the facts and the documents that were given to us,” Clavano said, referring to documents submitted to them by the House of Representatives, Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI) and the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).

“Pinakikinggan namin ho talaga siya (Bernardo) because he is a state witness and he has been cooperating with us. We do find him credible, and his statements are being used as leads to point us in the right direction. It's just that corruption is never meant to be seen in the limelight. Laging patago ‘yan. Not one paper trail will bear the signature of the person asking for the budget that is malversed. So, statements alone [by Bernardo] could be enough if it is corroborated also by other evidence,” Clavano added.

Bernardo made these allegations before the Senate Blue Ribbon panel inquiry on the flood control mess in 2025, and his allegations were also cited by Senator Panfilo Lacson, who had served as the Senate Blue Ribbon chairperson, in a privilege speech in November 2025.

Bernardo said then Executive Secretary Bersamin asked for a 15-percent commitment to the Office of the Executive Secretary related to P2.85 billion worth of projects that would utilize unprogrammed funds in the national budget, and that Olaivar asked for a list of projects.
Clavano, however, assured that the Ombudsman will only file cases based on evidence.

“We don't work in the sense that we have a target at hahabulin namin ng ebidensiya. Mauuna talaga ang ebidensiya. Wherever the evidence goes, we will follow. We cannot have a target and then look for evidence to support the case only for the sake of silencing critics. That's not how we do things here,” he said.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: What to expect at Alex Eala’s homecoming tennis event
articles.summary: Filipinos have followed Alex Eala through television broadcasts, news reports, and clips from tournaments around the world. Some have even traveled overseas to watch her compete. Her following keeps…

blocks.text: Lifestyle | Luminaries and Life
From young Filipino tennis players and celebrities to her match against Janice Tjen, here are the ticket prices, presale dates, and other details fans should know

Filipinos have followed Alex Eala through television broadcasts, news reports, and clips from tournaments around the world. Some have even traveled overseas to watch her compete. Her following keeps growing with each tournament. This December, Filipino fans will have the opportunity to see her play right here at home.
Alex Eala (Photo: Tatler Philippines)

“Alex Eala Live: Game. Set. Celebrate” will be held on Dec. 8, 2026, at the Philippine Arena in Bocaue, Bulacan. Created and organized by Tatler Sports and Entertainment, the homecoming celebration will feature young Filipino tennis players, a celebrity exhibition match, live performances, and Alex’s headline match against Janice Tjen.

During a press conference on Aug. 28, Michel Lamunière, chairman and CEO of Tatler Asia, and Irene Martel Francisco, managing director of Tatler Philippines, shared more details about the event and what fans can expect.

“Alex was really excited because, for her, this is a homecoming opportunity,” said Irene. “People are currently traveling abroad to watch her play, so this is their chance to see her live in the Philippines.”
Here are some of the things fans can expect.

blocks.caption: (Photo: Tatler Sports and Entertainment)

blocks.text: (Photo: Tatler Sports and Entertainment)
It will feature three tennis matches

The event will not be limited to Alex’s main match. “The first will feature young Filipino talents, followed by a game with celebrities, and the third will be the match between Alex and Janice,” Michel said.

The celebrity exhibition is expected to feature familiar Philippine personalities. Their identities have yet to be announced, but Michel promises an entertaining match. “They might not be as good as Alex at tennis, but they will bring passion and excitement.”
Youth development clinics, interactive fan activities, and live musical performances are also being planned.
Alex will face Janice Tjen in a potentially record-setting match
Alex’s opponent will be Janice Tjen of Indonesia, making the headline match an all-Southeast Asian contest between two young players competing internationally.

The pairing also gives regional tennis a rare spotlight in a venue of this size. The Philippine Arena has a maximum capacity of 55,000, although the number of seats available for the event will depend on its final tennis-court configuration.

The current record stands at 51,954 spectators, set during the 2020 Match in Africa exhibition between Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal in Cape Town. If the Dec. 8 crowd surpasses that number, Alex and Janice’s match could become the most attended tennis event in history.
Alex is involved in planning the experience

The event is not simply being arranged around Alex. She is also taking part in discussions about how the celebration will look and feel. Manila Bulletin Lifestyle asked how much input the tennis player has provided, to which Irene answered, “A lot. She is very involved in what it is going to look like and how it is going to feel.”

The complete theme and program have not been finalized, although Irene said audiences can expect Filipino cultural elements. “Nothing is final yet because we have just announced it. Rest assured that we will always take her wishes and input into consideration.”
This involvement could make the event feel more personal, giving audiences a celebration influenced by the athlete they have come to support.
Tickets will start at ₱600

Organizers say tickets will be offered at different price levels to make the event accessible to a wide audience. Prices will range from ₱600 for general admission to ₱25,000, with thousands of seats allocated to the general-admission section.

Fans may pre-register for tickets here until Sept. 6 at 11:59 p.m. Registered fans will have access to the presale beginning Sept. 7 at 12 p.m. until Sept. 13 at 11:59 p.m. General ticket sales will open on Sept. 14 at 12 p.m.

More details will be announced soon, including merchandise, performance lineup, match formats, and transportation arrangements. To know more, visit the event’s official ticketing page: https://bit.ly/AELWL26.

articles.title: Germany's grape harvest starts earlier than ever
articles.summary: Growers expect good quality but below-average yields following an exceptionally hot summer. It continues a decades-long shift toward earlier picking.

image.caption: Germany's grape harvest has begun exceptionally early this yearImage: Udo Herrmann/CHROMORANGE/picture alliance

blocks.text: Germany's main grape harvest has begun earlier than ever recorded after the country's exceptionally hot summer accelerated ripening across its wine-growing regions, the German Wine Institute said on Friday.
The record-early harvest continues a trend seen in recent decades, with higher temperatures affecting when grapes ripen, as well as their sugar and acidity levels.
Where and when is the harvest starting?
"This was the earliest start to the harvest ever in all wine-growing regions," institute spokesman Ernst Büscher said. "Some winegrowers even cut short their holidays because of it."
Harvesting is already underway across Germany's wine regions, from Saxony in the east to Lake Constance in the south.
The harvest has already included not only grapes for Federweisser — partially fermented young wine — and sparkling wine, but also the first grapes destined for premium wines.
The main harvest is expected to begin "on a large scale" in the first week of September.
Compared with recent years, the main harvest has begun around one to two weeks earlier, according to Büscher.
"Compared with 30 or 40 years ago, it is certainly four weeks earlier," he said.
Why is the harvest so early?
The hot, dry summer caused grapes to ripen unusually quickly, while many varieties are reaching maturity at roughly the same time.
That means the harvest is also expected to proceed rapidly and could be completed by the end of September.
"This will be a very fast harvest because almost all varieties are ripening at the same time," Büscher said.

Climate change has brought some advantages for Germany's wine industry over the years. Warmer conditions have allowed growers to experiment with grape varieties better suited to warmer climates and have made wine cultivation possible in some new areas.
DocFilm - Will Non-alcoholic Wine Save the Winemakers?
But increasingly long and frequent periods of heat and drought also pose challenges.
Growers are closely watching both sugar and acidity levels. Leaving grapes on the vines too long in hot conditions can push sugar levels higher, producing stronger wines with more alcohol.
High temperatures can also reduce the fruit acidity that gives many German white wines their characteristic freshness.
What will the 2026 vintage be like?
Growers are pleased with the quality of the grapes harvested so far.
"The grapes are still very healthy," Büscher said, adding that this pointed to aromatic white wines. Producers are also expecting deeply colored red wines.
However, the overall harvest is expected to be below average because dry conditions have left grapes smaller than usual.
Significant rainfall in the coming weeks could accelerate the harvest even further.
Edited by: Rob Turner
